gaps.what: The regions are distinguishable but inert. Zero discrete sound events across 21 minutes 20 seconds of ambience in 64 recordings; crest factor never exceeds 17.4 dB anywhere.
gaps.why_it_matters: Region identity is currently carried entirely by the colour of a steady hum. A player standing still anywhere in the world hears nothing occur, and the axis on which players actually recognise a place - what happens in it - is empty. It also makes the B2 check easy for the wrong reason (AUDB2-F10).

gaps.what: The round's headline measurements were taken in a world with nobody in it and no longer reproduce on the build that ships. machine.js:472 added a giver-presence term to open() — `giver absent: <npc> is not in this world`, gate 'giver_presence', with presenceMode defaulting to 'on' at machine.js:93 — after the round-2 numbers were taken. Neither faction-probe.mjs nor faction-seam-probe.mjs calls questPresenceGate, and both boot a bare world. Re-running the builder's own tool with its own command line takes the Wet Ledger from the 16/16 recorded on disk to 8/16: P3 7/18 quests offerable (was 18/18), P4 top derived rank 4 (was 7), P13 the seat is NOT vacated by play, P14 rank-7-and-non-violent FAIL, P15 17 questOpen calls refused, and P16 — the round's strongest claim — flips from 'the walk wrote no reputation at all; 398 was paid entirely by the quests' own consequences' to 'the walk WROTE reputation 10, 22, 36, 52, 70, 90, 112'. The cascade is causal: because open() refuses, faction-probe's grantRep() fallback fires to satisfy rank terms by hand, so the no-reputation-writes property was never independent of the gate.
gaps.remedy: Make faction-probe.mjs and faction-seam-probe.mjs boot an inhabited state, or call questPresenceGate('report') and publish the miss list. Then re-run all three lines and EXPECT the report to change — a probe that returns 16/16 unchanged is still not standing in the world. Until then no reports/faction-probe-*.json figure may be cited, including every headline in orchestration/status/W1-FACTIONS-r2.json.

gaps.what: The blind pack cannot separate quality from provenance, and each round's fix creates the next round's tell. r1 leaked setting nouns (17/17); r4 masked them and now leaks mask density (15/15).
gaps.why_it_matters: Every prose verdict that cites a blind pack score is citing a provenance score wearing a quality label. The next masking fix will leak something else, because the two corpora differ in shape, not just in labels.
remedy: Reject any trio whose two sides differ in '[NAME-' count by more than ~15%; equalise by inserting mask tokens into the sparser side, or drop to a single unindexed opaque token.
Fix the masker's word boundaries — the dropped-text corruption in 14/15 reference files is a correctness bug independent of blinding.
Segregate registers by artifact class: compare our journal entries to Morrowind books, or build a 'functional text' register judged on unambiguity rather than voice.
Sample reference passages matched on proper-noun density, not just on length.
Run the owed M5 second pass with the harsher lens on the trios where the pick was ours.

gaps.what: Our characters do not address the player. Questions at 0.2x the reference, exclamations at 0.6x, first person at 0.5x, and every line closes on an epigram instead of a want. The world is narrated AT the player by 300 speakers who share one wit and none of whom is curious about them.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every other finding is downstream of it. The 'eleven' filler, the 'Which' fragments and the punchline uniformity are all symptoms of prose optimised sentence-by-sentence rather than written for a person who wants something. It is also the only tell that no find-and-replace can touch, and the one a reader finds in four lines.
remedy: GATE IT. check-content.mjs: per dialogue file, question marks >= 40 per 10k and -body forms = 0. Loud warning now, hard fail from wave 2. Without a check that RUNS, section 5 happens again within hours — it already has, twice.
FIX THE PACK BEFORE THE NEXT JUDGEMENT. Name-substitute both sides in build-r2-packs.mjs; switch to RI-MTH03 sec D's quality question. One afternoon of tool work, no writing.

AUTHORING, NOT FIND-AND-REPLACE. For every topic with three infos, one info must be the NPC asking the player something and reacting to what they are. This is the only fix for TELL-1 and TELL-2 and it is the work the martial library should be doing now.
DO NOT push SR-01 further. The builder is right that the residue lives in keepers, archivists and the court, calibrated formal on purpose. Moving it means making the game worse to move a number.
evidence: 10 blind dialogue trials: 4 question marks ours vs 76 reference; 0 exclamations ours vs 3.
A one-token rule 'fewer question marks = ours' scores 9/10 with one tie — stronger than 'eleven' ever was and contraction-blind.
SR-05 live: 24.43 vs 158.83 per 10k = 0.2x, essentially unmoved by the 180-line pass (19.26 -> 24.99 -> 24.43).
55-utility.json and 50-factions.json, both authored AFTER the pass: 2.7 and 2.5 question marks per 10k, zero exclamations across 7,648 words.

gaps.what: The RI-WLD12 M68 blind pack cannot answer the question it exists to ask, because the camera is standing inside the scenery. Of 24 frames shipped, 16 have a foreground boulder within a few metres of the lens and 5 are unreadable; I answered 'two places' on 52.6% of usable frames against an 80% bar, and the >=25%-'one' fail clause fired at 47.4%. Stratified by whether the lens was blocked, the two-rate is 75.0% on the 8 unoccluded frames and 36.4% on the 11 usable occluded ones. The pose is computed in node at the crossover coordinate with no occlusion test, and the province scatters its props in the renderer from noise, so nothing on the node side knows what is in front of the lens. The pack is also half-built — the builder's process died at 24 of 48 frames, so KEY.json and QUESTION.md were never written — and the frames are 1280x720 where M68 specifies 1920x1080.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the check that decides whether the piece's headline bar is met at all, and seam S35 raised its stakes: the map now shows only terrain already travelled, so it cannot tell a player where they are going, and region identity has to carry that load alone. The measurement currently cannot be cited in either direction — it is not evidence that the borders fail, and it is not evidence that they work. Worse, the builder itself wrote the warning that predicts this exactly in its round-2 handover — 'at a border the flora is dense BY CONSTRUCTION, and nothing on the node side knows what is between the lens and the subject, since the scatter happens in the renderer from noise' — after losing two frames to it, and then built the pack tool without carrying that lesson into it. The same lesson was lost twice inside one piece. The positive half of the result should not be lost either: where a border IS visible, zero frames were decided by fog or colour and six of ten by a built object, so RI-WLD12's 'fog border' failure mode and S24's 'a region only distinguishable by fog colour is a defect' do not occur anywhere in this pack.

remedy.action: Add an occlusion test to tools/world/wld12-blind-pack.mjs: before accepting a pose, cast from the eye toward the intended subject and reject or re-place any pose with geometry inside the first 4 m, reusing the --candidates=N sweep threshold-shots.mjs already has. Shoot at 1920x1080 as M68 specifies, complete all 48 frames, write KEY.json into a sibling wld12-blind.reveal/ directory rather than inside the pack, and remove the scoring rule from QUESTION.md so the judge is not told which cue loses.
remedy.acceptance: 48 frames at 1920x1080, no more than 4 of them with geometry inside 4 m of the lens; KEY.json outside the pack directory; QUESTION.md silent on scoring; and a fresh judge who did not build the pack answers >=80% 'two' with >=70% naming an object or a landform. Re-running the same judgement on the CURRENT 24 frames must still reproduce 52.6%, so the change is demonstrably the camera and not the scoring.

gaps.what: The waterline drawn on the player's body is live and correct to about 0.07 m — I measured it climbing calf to thigh to waist across a 1.178 m tide swing at one fixed point and camera, 21,804 changed pixels every one of which is on the character. The water surface it is a line OF is not. (a) game/src/world/province.js:747-773 builds each tile's water mesh on a 12.5 m lattice and drops any quad with a single dry corner, so on the paddy-and-channel tile both rounds photographed it keeps 32.1% of quads over ground that is 61.3% wet — and the shot point's own quad, corners [1.650, 1.600, null, null], is dropped: no water is drawn on the square metre the player stands in, in 0.886 m of it. (b) Where water IS drawn the mesh is sampled at tile-build time and nothing rebuilds it when the tide moves: moving the tide changes 21,804 pixels and not one of them is ground, while forcing a rebuild at the same tide changes 657,561. (c) The 20 s drying window §10.3 requires does not exist at all — a body dry throughout and the same body one second out of 1.05 m of water are BYTE-IDENTICAL, md5 8531d20d4f3dc7f82b8b6be2b9c63a77, because esBand is a world-space cutoff that the body rises above the moment it steps up a bank.
gaps.why_it_matters: RI-WLD10 §10.3 calls the waterline 'the player's only depth readout and it is not optional' and §1 forbids a HUD substitute, so a player standing hip-deep sees darkened legs on green grass with no water in the frame, and after a tide swing sees a body wet to the chest with the drawn water at their ankles — which is the readout S25 made S18's permanent third person load-bearing for.

remedy.action: Three changes, all local. (1) province.js:756 — stop dropping a water quad because one corner is dry: emit the quad whenever ANY corner is wet, clamping each dry corner's y down to the local ground height, so a channel narrower than the 12.5 m lattice still gets a surface that meets the bank. (2) Mark province tiles water-dirty when field.tidePhase crosses a threshold and rewrite only the water sub-mesh's vertex Y from waterSurfaceAt() — the per-region geometry already exists per tile, so this is a position-attribute update, not a tile rebuild. (3) renderer.js _playerWaterline() — while drying, carry uWaterY relative to the body: hold the offset between the surface and the player's foot height at the moment the band left W0 rather than a frozen world Y, so stepping up a bank keeps the wet band on the legs and it fades over the declared window.
remedy.acceptance: (1) A capture at (2226.9, 4376.1) shows a drawn water surface meeting the body at the height the shader shades to. (2) probe-water-quad-coverage.mjs reports kept-quad fraction >= 0.90 x wet-area fraction on tiles (2100,4200) and (2400,4200), against today's 32.1%/61.3% and 62.0%/85.0%. (3) The LOW->HIGH pair at (2620,4362) changes ground pixels as well as body pixels with NO forced rebuild in ops. (4) The matched drying pair stops being byte-identical, and a capture 19 s after leaving water still shows wet-shading while one at 21 s does not.
remedy.owner_hint: W1-03 with W1-01 — (1) and (2) are in province.js which W1-01 owns; land them together so the waterline and the water agree.

gaps.what: RUSH is gated on a distance band (dist > 5.0*omega) rather than on whether the distance is actually closing, and APPROACH advances at archetype.*.walk_mps, which for INFANTRY is 2.20 m/s against a player walk of 2.00 m/s. An enemy 10 m from a player walking away in a straight line closes at 0.20 m/s, NEVER enters RUSH in 1,800 frames, never gets nearer than 8.14 m, reaches its 32 m hard leash, oscillates REPOSITION<->LEASH_RETURN for 235 frames at the boundary and walks home. Five of the seven fighting statblocks never enter RUSH against a walking player. The enemy does WORSE against a walking player than a jogging one, because walking keeps the gap just under the band boundary that would trigger a sprint.

gaps.what: RI-PRG04's own Comparison method #8, 'Clock consequence', has never been run. It is four assertions and it is written out in the item: "Rest at in-game 17:00. ASSERT the clock reads 23:00, the night roster is active, merchants are closed, and any active timed quest has consumed 6 hours. Rest 4x in a row: ASSERT the clock advances 24 h and returns to the same shop state." Across three rounds the aggregation has measured exactly the first clause — rest moves the clock 12.005093 -> 18.005093, exactly 6 h — and none of the other five. No round has checked a roster, a merchant, a schedule, a quest deadline or the four-rest round trip. That axis is scored 'Clock cost', its 10 rung is 'full consequence chain fires' and its 6 rung is 'clock advances AND ROSTER SWAPS', so on evidence it cannot rise above 6 and it is the min over the item's eight axes. This round made the axis matter more, not less: it shipped a new clock model (Environment.step holds the clock while a death is in flight, RI-PRG04 §6 rule 4) whose own CONSUMPTION arm reports T5_consumer_moved: false — reports/runs/W1-13-R3/clock.json names sim/settlement.js#isOpen and sim/npc.js#slotAt in its header, then reads getEnvironment().phase (which returns 'night' on both sides of its comparison) and getWorldStats().settlement (null, because that report has no such key), and ships the false. Under ARBITRATION.md §3 a model with no demonstrated consumer is unmeasurable => 0.
gaps.why_it_matters: It is the axis holding RI-PRG04 at 6 and therefore the whole piece below the gate, and it is the Morrowind half of the entire hearth contract — the item's own bar says resting 'carries a Morrowind consequence that a bonfire never had: it moves the world's clock, and the world notices'. Nothing in the measured build shows the world noticing. It is not far away either: I drove one of the six consequences in four deaths and one kill. With the round's clock fix in place, 4 deaths at 20:58 leave the clock at 20.967593 and one ordinary inf_trash pays 42 souls; with the fix deleted the same 4 deaths walk the clock to 21.023148, across sim/souls.js's NIGHT_FROM_H = 21, and the same kill pays 57 = round(42 x 1.35). That is a world-side consumer changing an entity's behaviour, it took one query, and it says something the round did not notice: under round 2's clock, DYING REPEATEDLY WAS A WAY TO FARM THE NIGHT RATE, which is the loss-compensation shape RI-JRN06 D9 and AR-1 exist to forbid. The fix is worth more than the round claimed for it, and the method that would have shown that has been sitting in the item, unrun, since round 1.

gaps.what: Engine._restoreFightFromSave() clears _equipLoadPinned, and game/src/save/fight.js persists fight.loadout.equip_load_pct which nothing ever reads back. A scenario that DECLARES its equip load therefore keeps it across a loadState() and loses it across a save. Round 3's new hands term (+9.5 kg for the default loadout) makes the recomputed answer land on the other side of the 30% cliff. Measured live, hostiles on the floor, nothing despawned: arena_duel with a shell-scale-hauberk and legion-greaves on reads 24.000000% / LIGHT / 26 i-frames / 22 f@60 recovery / 52 f@60 total before saveRoundTrip() and 33.424658% / MEDIUM / 22 i-frames / 34 recovery / 60 total after it. arena_flat gives the identical pair. Bare, arena_duel goes 24.000000% -> 13.013699%, same tier but still not the saved number. The counterfactual is round 3's OWN delete-the-fix switch: with __breakW116('hands') the same save and the same reload land at 20.410959%, LIGHT, 26 i-frames, so the hands term is exactly what crosses the cliff.
gaps.why_it_matters: arena_duel and arena_flat are the fixtures W1-09, W1-10 and W1-11 calibrate combat in, and round 3's stated safety argument is that those states pin their equip load so the calibration is `untouched, byte for byte`. That holds at load and fails after a save, so no equip-load-dependent measurement taken after a save/load anywhere in this project is trustworthy. From the player's chair it is worse and simpler: quit during a boss fight, resume, and your dodge is four frames shorter and 8 frames longer to recover from, with nothing having changed in the world. Seam S23 gives RI-CMB01 the i-frame count outright, and an in-fight number that changes across a reload is the one thing that ruling exists to protect. It is also RULES #7 verbatim — a field written into the save and never read back — and it is the shape round 3's own D4 probe was written to catch, missed because the probe loads 49 states and saves none.

gaps.what: Engine._recomputeEquipLoad() implements RI-PRG07 §2's formula minus its first two terms. §2 reads `equipRatio = (weight of equipped weapons, shields, armour, talismans) / maxLoad`; the producer iterates sim.inventory and sums the carried.json weight of rows carrying a `slot`. The weapon the fight swings is combat.player.weaponId, set by CombatSystem.setLoadout() from loadout.weapon, and is not an inventory row; neither is the shield. Measured live on one fixture: a character holding ssw_garrison_sword and marsh_oak_medium reads 0.000000%; equipping a bog-iron-maul through the real equip queue moves the ratio to 15.753425% AND LEAVES combat.player.weapon AT ssw_garrison_sword; setLoadout({weapon:'ultra-greatsword', shield:'greatshield_xanmeer'}) then leaves the ratio at 15.753425%, unchanged to six decimal places. There are two right hands — one that is weighed and one that fights — which is RULES 10's `two parallel implementations of one system`, the same shape this round found for sprint and walked past for the weapon. The weight is not missing from the tree: game/data/weapons/classes.json ships an `equip_weight` column on all fifteen classes (Dagger 1 ... Ultra greatsword 20), combat/moveset.js:187 copies it onto the move table, and nothing in game/src ever reads it. The shields block carries guard angle and parry windows and no weight column at all, while RI-PRG07 §4 declares buckler 4 / kite 9 / greatshield 18.
gaps.why_it_matters: It is the round's own headline, narrowed until it is nearly untrue from the player's chair. `Encumbrance now moves the roll from the world` holds only for five clothing slots whose heaviest legal contents total 16.8 kg = 23.01% of the base sheet, which is LIGHT — so MEDIUM is unreachable by armour, not just HEAVY and OVERLOADED as reported, and the builder's own headline arm crosses the 30% cliff entirely on the strength of an 11.5 kg maul sitting in a slot the fight does not read. RI-PRG07's whole tuning target for the 30% breakpoint (`the Fence's one extra armour piece costs them Light`) and its §5 six-build regression fixture cannot be instantiated. And it is fixable without inventing a single weight: counting the declared weapon class weight moves the base sheet from 43.54% to 56.62%, most of the way to the HEAVY cliff on shipped data alone.

In Engine._recomputeEquipLoad(), add this.combat.player.moves.equip_weight (already carried by combat/moveset.js:187) and the shield's weight into `w`, beside the inventory `slot` sum. Do not touch the divisor — _equipCapacity() is correct and the two-name split must survive. 2. Add a `weight` field to every row of game/data/weapons/classes.json's `shields` block from RI-PRG07 §4: buckler 4, small 4, medium 9, greatshield 18, parry_tool 1. 3. Make Engine._finishEquipCommit(), on a row whose slot resolves to 'right' or 'left', call setLoadout({weapon}) / setLoadout({shield}) so the hand that is weighed and the hand that fights are one object — this is the RULES 10 half and it is what stops the defect returning. 4. Add equip_load.weapon_weight, equip_load.shield_weight and equip_load.overloaded_denies_sprint to getBurden()'s consumer table, and implement the third (RI-CMB01 §B) at the same action gate sim/player.js already uses for worldDeny.sprint. 5. Seed _equipLoadBase to the computed base on the frame the producer first engages, BEFORE applying any delta, so a live Feather (magnitude 30) or Burden (magnitude 40) offset is not destroyed by the first equip and then subtracted a second time by its own _undo.

gaps.what: RI-AUD03 §A's 'Level (rel. bed)' band is a claim about EVENTS, and every mechanism that touches it is a per-layer median: gate O3 grades the median of a bed/layer's events, and the corrective trim `event_gain_db` is a single number per layer, while the second gain stage it corrects (`synth.gain_db`, -5..-13) varies PER EVENT. A per-layer trim cannot in principle unbury an event quieter than its layer-mates; it can only move the whole spread. The result is that the round-1 defect this piece exists to close -- declared in band, buried by a second gain stage -- is still present for individual events while the gate reports zero failures: 54 of 413 measured events sit outside §A's band with the tool's own +/-2 dB tolerance, 33 of them buried below the floor, in 11 of 33 bed/layer pairs whose median passes.
gaps.why_it_matters: The buried events are not marginal ones. blackwood/L3/distant_axe renders at -23.1 dB relative to the bed -- 15 dB below §A's floor -- and 'distant axe-strokes' is one of the three sounds that bed's own `brief` field advertises. deep-marshes/L3/marsh_gas_release reaches -30.4 dB. well/L3/stone_shift -16.3, dungeon/L3/block_settle -11.1. From the player's chair those sounds do not exist, which is exactly the state the B2 judge described as 'nothing ever happens in any of them' and exactly the state this round was commissioned to end. Because the gate is green, no future round has a reason to look.

remedy.action: Gate O3 on EVERY measured event rather than on the layer median -- the check is already written and falsifiable at tools/audio/critic-w1-22-r2-bands.mjs B1, which goes red on the shipped tree, redder under --sabotage widen, and GREEN under --sabotage centre (every event collapsed onto its layer median), proving its reading is about the spread and not about the level. Then give the trim the same granularity as the stage it corrects: calibrate a per-EVENT gain rather than one `event_gain_db` per layer, since the quantity being corrected varies per event. Both halves are small and neither needs new engine code.

gaps.what: The piece diagnosed the province's worst authorial habit exactly right — 'a province that only ever says lease has adopted the Provincial Office's vocabulary as narration' — and prescribed exactly the right remedy: 'the euphemism must be somebody's POSITION and not the world's voice'. CF-D008 was then registered with two positions, and BOTH are voiced in dialogue by the coloniser. Position A is an Imperial clerk: 'No subject of the Empire may be held as property inside the Empire's law. Where it happens it happens outside that law, off foreign keels, and the Office has made representations. I've copied three of them myself.' Position B is a House Dres slave-factor: 'The House keeps a stock column and people are entered in it and taken out of it, and the law you are quoting changes the word on the paper and nothing else.' Both books voicing B are Dunmer and Imperial hands — a salt-factor's ledger and marginalia in a borrowed Imperial address. Of 347 people in the province, 227 are Argonian; 66 of those have any answer to the topic `slavery`; between them they give three distinct sentences, and the only one written for an Argonian mouth is untagged and is a refusal to speak: 'This one will not discuss it with you standing there, and this one is sorry.' Carrying no `cf`, it contributes nothing to the 27-of-27 census, nothing to the 43/43 perturbation, and nothing to the register. Meanwhile CF-D008/B's held_by names 'every soul who has been on the Blackrose roll' and its machine holders list `dres-factor, sapcutter, mudborn, outlaw` — of which only dres-factor has a line. The registry credits the enslaved with a position and the build gives them no sentence. And the ruling on this dispute, which the registry's own note calls 'the province's central moral fact', is one of the nine that recover from the shipped bytes in three guesses.
gaps.why_it_matters: RI-LOR06 §1.2 forbids the world from correcting a contradiction, and §2 gives held_by one job: to stop a dispute nobody actually holds. Both rules are satisfied on paper and inverted in practice. The register was built to move the euphemism from narration into somebody's mouth; it moved it into two colonists' mouths and left the people it is about exactly where they were, which is silent. That is not a small authorial miss — it is the difference between a province that depicts a colonial vocabulary and a province that has adopted one, and RI-LOR01's 'How we lose' #7 names precisely this failure ('Imperial contempt swallowed whole ... the game must know the difference even when the book does not'). It is also the piece's own thesis failing on its own headline example, which is the strongest possible argument that the register's 0.019% behavioural footprint is a real limit and not a technicality.

gaps.what: The sabotage facility fails when its arms agree, and whether it can SEE that they agree is delegated to `support` - a caller-supplied field that is optional, undefined by default, unvalidated, and whose two honest readings give opposite verdicts on the strongest real inert control on this tree. W1-14-r3's shipped `--break=nocast`, which a human critic ruled inert, comes back OK when support is 'effects examined' (55/55), VACUOUS when it is 'effects delivered' (55/0), and OK again when the caller omits support entirely. Four further holes in the same cascade: two arms whose value is `undefined` canonicalise to agreement and return INERT (a confident claim about a measurement that never happened - I hit this by accident on my first run, against a real artifact); MASKED is last in the cascade and is shadowed by any unmet margin or wrong direction; armsAgree is decided on intact-vs-all-broken alone, so a control with a demonstrably live factor is reported INERT under cancellation while the same record lists that factor as moving it; and the documented obligation on the `supportArms:'intact'` escape hatch (a caller 'must say why, in support_note') is enforced nowhere and support_note is not even copied onto the result, so the canonical W1-13 failure passes with a one-key spec change.
gaps.why_it_matters: This piece exists to make the project's most common failure detectable, and PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC §10 names 'the control is never run' as the most likely failure in the corpus. Every one of the five holes above is that same failure occurring inside the facility built to catch it. Worse for adoption: the facility is meant to be used by other pieces, and the first thing a new caller writes is measure(). Two of the three ways a careful engineer would fill in `support` cause the facility to pass an inert control, and the third - omitting it - is the default.

remedy.action: Four changes, all in tools/experience/lib/sabotage.mjs. (1) MAKE SUPPORT MANDATORY: runControl already throws on a spec with no factors ('a control with no factors is not a control'); throw the same way when any arm returns no finite support - a control that cannot say what it ranged over is not a control. Amend the docstring's 'the number of units the measurement ranged over' to 'units that REACHED THE COMPARATOR', which is the single word separating A1 from A2. (2) ADD `NO_MEASUREMENT`: when every arm's value canonicalises to 'null', say that instead of INERT - the same argument the file already makes for VACUOUS. (3) ADD `SHORT_CIRCUIT` for the fourth failure shape, fired when the broken arm's support collapses relative to the intact arm's; both numbers are already on every arm record. (4) FIX THE CASCADE: hoist `masked` above the margin and direction tests, make armsAgree read `distinct_values === 1` (computed one line above), and throw when supportArms:'intact' arrives with no support_note, carrying that note onto the result so a report can list every control that opted out.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run `node tools/experience/critic-w1-25.mjs --a --b` against the amended facility. A1 and A3 must become ERROR or NO_MEASUREMENT rather than OK; A4 must become NO_MEASUREMENT; B-COLLIDE-1 must become MASKED; B-COLLIDE-2 must stop being INERT; B-COLLIDE-4 must throw. `--self-test` 6/6, the three existing facility breaks and `--cases` 8/8 must all still pass, and a FOURTH facility break `--break=support-optional` must be added and shown going red. The acceptance harness is already on the tree and does not need writing.

gaps.what: Engine._titleApply('new') — the row the title's `New` commits to — calls censusBegin({}) with no options. Census.spec.race is set by exactly one function, Census.observe(race), called from exactly one place: censusBegin, when opts.race is present. So on the player's path race is never observed, and Census.answer() at writ.race-observed throws 'race must be observed before the scene reaches the desk'. _censusApplyPending() catches it, emits census_refused and draws the reason on the surface, so the player is left in front of the Warden-Scribe reading an engine error string as dialogue, with no way forward and no way out of the room (the Writ House door is held until you are written down).
gaps.why_it_matters: Every number this piece has ever published — DTR 0.982, AC 6 of 7, NAMED 14 of 14, the writ carried out, 61.5 s of body before the first question — was taken on a scene that only the harness can open, because the harness supplies the one creation input the player never gives. NEXT-DISPATCH §P calls this piece the binding gate for handing the owner a playable build; a person who clones this repo, serves it and presses New cannot make a character or reach the world. The corpus's own driver reproduces the defect and cannot see it: journey-run.mjs opens with censusBegin({}) too and walks the scene inside `catch { break; }`, so it reports M4 clause 1 as 'N/A — no character-field-writing event in the trace' instead of as a failure.

remedy.action: Observe the race of the body the player is actually in at the moment `New` begins the scene. RI-CHR01 §1 row 2 is explicit that race is observed and never asked, so the value must come from the body — which means the choice of that body is W1-07's and must exist before this can be done honestly. A hardcoded default would satisfy the acceptance test below and betray the item, so the acceptance names that too. Separately, replace journey-run.mjs's bare `catch { break; }` at the census walk with a recorded failure, so the driver can never again report an absence as N/A.

gaps.what: installSurfaceShader() computes the world height its wetness mask rides on as `vEsSurfaceWorldY=(modelMatrix*vec4(transformed,1.0)).y`, inserted after `#include <begin_vertex>`. three.js applies `instanceMatrix` in `project_vertex`, which runs later — its own `worldpos_vertex` chunk is `worldPosition = instanceMatrix * worldPosition; worldPosition = modelMatrix * worldPosition;`. So every instance of an InstancedMesh is handed the base geometry's height and the whole mesh shares one position on the wetness ramp. Measured with a saturating band: two separate Meshes at y -1.2 and y +1.2 separate by 0.02393 in mean luminance (the high quad moving by precisely 0.00000, i.e. fully dry, as it must); two INSTANCES at the same two heights separate by 0.00150 — 6% of the control. Reproduced identically on SwiftShader (0.023926 / 0.001497) and on an RTX A4500 (0.023896 / 0.001511). The same line also omits `batchingMatrix` and is taken before `skinning_vertex`.
gaps.why_it_matters: The shipped world's live census counts 377 InstancedMeshes carrying 31143 instances, drawn from the families bark, leaf, reed and stone — the trunks, canopies, reeds and rocks that fill a Black Marsh frame. setWorldWetness() is published as W1-30B's rain consumer and is the mechanism by which 'B's rain lands on materials rather than on fog'. It currently lands on everything except the marsh. No arm of the builder's own proof could see it: tools/assets/rig/family-closeup.html wetnessProof() renders one non-instanced plane at the origin, where modelMatrix * transformed IS the world position, so all five families and both the wet and dry arms fabricated the same untested input.

remedy.action: One narrow commit in game/src/render/visual-foundation.js plus the matching two rows of game/src/render/MATERIAL_API.md. PRESERVE: the whole authored library, the 20-family registry, FAMILY_SET, the detail-normal blend, the wear mask and its wearFrom axis, the magenta fallback, the palette swatches, and every existing option key and its meaning — the freeze is additive-only and nothing here removes or repurposes an option. gaps.what: The visible body of every character in the game is an assembly of primitive solids rather than a built figure, and the numbers say so on both axes at once. Shoulders are glossy ellipsoids attached to a flat rectangular torso plate; the pelvis is a trapezoid; limbs are tapered cones; the player's legs terminate in points with no foot. The face carries 1 of 7 landmarks (a crest root, and nothing else — no brow ridge, orbit rim, naris, cheek-to-jaw line, mandible line or chin underside). The whole shipped roster is 5.87-6.84 heads tall (median 6.58) against RI-VIS10 C1's 7.0-8.0 band, with 0 of 41 figures inside it. The player is 15142 triangles against RI-VIS08 B2's 25000 and the creature 4834 against 12000. The skin opens 289 crack pixels across 179 of 640 posed frames at the calf/foot and head/hand seams. The art family that carries 329 of 408 NPCs has no eye geometry at all. Crucially this is NOT a rig defect: the same build passes RI-VIS08 C1, C3, C4, C6, C7, C8 and C9 with foot slide at 6 mm against a 30 mm bar, root-motion r = 1.0000, grip error 0.000 m and foot IK holding 100% of planted frames on a 20-degree slope and on stairs.
gaps.why_it_matters: It is the reason the owner, playing the game, said the player character and every NPC look frankly ridiculous — a viewer identifies an ellipsoid stuck to a slab in the first half-second, before texture, light or animation is considered at all.

Driving all 19 census nodes through window.__HARNESS and screenshotting after each at 1920x1080 produces 20 byte-identical PNGs (sha256 7277a273453ac8631c318f3d9120d7b12b7f562b187adabf59fe3ca7b5daaeb5) showing a body standing in an empty green field: no barge hold, no Writ House interior, no Jeeh-Ei, no Warden-Scribe Tuleeh-Ma, no question, no answer options, and document.body.innerText empty at every node. listEntities() returns 0 entities before and after creation. The scene exists only as a JSON state machine whose getCensusState() self-reports full_screen:false, world_visible:true and full_screen_panels:0 — three fields with no rendered counterpart. gaps.why_it_matters: A player starting this game is never asked anything by anybody: the best-written material in the piece — a bored official who guesses your race wrong and tells you the sex box changes nothing because he has watched for eleven years — is delivered to no one, so character creation cannot be experienced at all.

gaps.what: The only guard in the build cannot attack and surrenders for nothing: guard_legion declares ai 'hold_ground' (combat/enemy.js only runs an action for ai === 'scripted', so an AGGRO guard held at 2.0 m for 900 frames deals 0 damage and never leaves REPOSITION) and its parley declares gold_price 0 against base_disposition 35, which makes combat/parley.js's GOLD ground unconditional — so one `interact` press yields a band-3 attack-on-sight guard at full HP for 0 gold and 0 stamina, leaving the imperial bounty at 3000 and jail null.
gaps.why_it_matters: Everything else this piece built downstream of a crime — the 17-crime schedule, the derived witness, the five report routes, the three-band ladder, the three arrest answers, the jail ledger, S6 persistence — is correct, measured and reachable, and all of it is discarded by a single button press against an enemy that could not have hurt you anyway. From the player's chair crime has no consequence, which is the exact failure RI-CRM01 exists to prevent and the exact shape RI-MTH07 warns about one level up: the model is computed, consumed, and then thrown away by the interaction that resolves it. It also makes ARBITRATION S13's non-lethal exit meaningless as a design object — a parley that always succeeds is not a choice, and the round-1 finding that the guard ladder was 'a function of a number setBounty() wrote' is only half closed: the band is now real behaviour, and the behaviour is nothing.

gaps.what: Four instruments now guard the one defect that has already been fixed (an untracked module plainly imported by `import … from`), while six deployment failure classes have zero instruments: a transient 5xx on the module graph, cache headers and a returning visitor, HTTP/2, the CDN's TLS as a browser sees it, a slow connection, and whether the Pages build ran at all. Two of those six — a warm cache on a second visit, and a slow connection — are precisely the conditions the owner's phone was in when it showed a black screen. Meanwhile the instruments that do exist fail in the direction of the tester: verify-playable's control is red because of its own screenshots (boot 10.7 s unobserved vs 69.7 s observed, slower in 3 of 3 paired runs, 3 of 6 screenshots timing out); verify-live-site's staleness check hashes against the dirty working tree rather than HEAD (3 of 60 sampled files differ from the worktree, 0 from HEAD) and looks at 2 of 715 files; and the aggregation that would run them all together is called by nothing.
gaps.why_it_matters: The owner opens the link on a phone on a real network for the second time; every instrument in this project has only ever measured a cold first load on a fast local wire, so the next black screen is as invisible as the first two were.

(2) Point verify-live-site's staleness check at HEAD (`git show HEAD:game/<rel>`) rather than `readFileSync(game/<rel>)`, widen it from 2 files to index.html + data/index.json + every .js under src/ and vendor/, and give it and check-image-refs the 5xx retry that verify-links.mjs already has. (3) Wire tools/playability/standing-check.mjs into tools/bank.mjs as a non-blocking post-push follow-up, and add check-image-refs and loader-retry to it. Then, and only then, add the missing class: one instrument that loads the deployed page twice with the cache warm between visits.

gaps.what: An enemy attack's swept volume does not cover the attacker's own root translation, so it cannot hit a target standing inside its forward root travel. Measured on a stationary player against a stationary champion_hist_marked in arena_champion, sweeping 0.0-4.0 m in 0.1 m steps: the chop hits from 1.2 m to 3.6 m and misses at EVERY distance from 0.0 to 1.1 m; the thrust hits 1.6-4.0 m and misses 0.0-1.5 m; combo_a hits 1.1-2.9 m and misses 0.0-1.0 m. Those minimum distances are the attacks' declared root_dz_m of 1.2 / 1.6 / 0.9. Zeroing root_dz_m moves the inner boundary to 0.6 / 0.8 / 0.8 m, confirming the root translation is the cause (data file reverted, git clean). The player's own weapons have no such hole — dagger, straight sword, spear, greatsword and halberd all hit from 0.0 m. The consequence, measured: a player who stands completely still at 0.8-1.1 m and does nothing but mash the light attack kills the 2876-HP champion in 1153-1377 frames taking ZERO damage, while the enemy completes 44-54 frames of live hitbox and suffers zero stagger frames. This is also the mechanical cause of the exemplar's headline out-of-band row: 141 of 211 enemy swings resolve as WHIFF, and 35 swings across five fights had the player invulnerable for every active frame at 0.01-0.60 m — inside the hole, where the swing could not have connected anyway, so i-frame negation reads 0.111 against a band of 0.40-0.80.
gaps.why_it_matters: The correct way to fight this game's boss is to walk inside it and stand still, which makes rolling, spacing, stamina and the entire i-frame system that RI-CMB01 gets exactly right decorative.

remedy.action: Sweep the attacker's root translation as well as its animated pose. RI-CMB04 §A's step order runs 5 (consume root motion) before 8 (sweep + query, this frame's pose vs last frame's); the sweep must interpolate the weapon socket capsule between last frame's WORLD-space pose and this frame's WORLD-space pose — root delta included — and the SUBSTEPS count must be derived from the larger of the arc travel and the root travel, not from the arc alone. A root_dz_m of 1.2 m spread over a 10-frame active window is 0.12 m per frame, which is inside one capsule radius, so the fix is a space change rather than a substep increase; verify both. Then re-derive SUBSTEPS from the measured maximum of (per-frame tip travel, per-frame root travel).

game/data/combat/hitgeometry.json (the `sweep` block and its substep rationale)

gaps.what: The round-2 hole in the weapon volume is untouched; it has been covered by a second volume that pays the weapon's damage. Ablation, measured on a copy of the loaded data with no file edited: delete `hitgeometry.json §body_hazard` and the champion's minimum reaching distance against a stationary player returns to chop 1.2 m, thrust 1.6 m, combo_a 1.1 m, combo_b 1.2 m — round 2's numbers to the decimal. With the block present, every hit inside those radii carries `via: "body"`, and a body hit deals the attack's full weapon damage: chop 96 at 0.05 m via body is the same 96 as at 3.65 m via weapon, thrust 75, combo_a 63. It is the same on the player's side — the dagger's blade cannot cut inside 0.75 m and the straight sword's inside 0.80 m, so 14 of the dagger's 19 connecting distances and 15 of the straight sword's 36 are torso-checks. Two of the seven player classes fail S26's contiguity clause outright, and the gaps sit exactly at the seam between the two volumes: the spear's body corridor stops at 1.15 m and its blade starts at 1.30 m, leaving 1.20-1.25 m dead; the halberd's stops at 1.10 m and starts at 1.35 m, leaving 1.15-1.30 m dead. Reproduced identically in headless Chromium and in the node arena. And it is what the fight is made of: in the shipping game, 5 to 7 of the 8 blows that kill a motionless player are `via: body`.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player who walks inside the champion watches a 1.75 m greatsword sweep over their head and loses 96 hit points to the chest that walked through them, and a spearman standing at 1.22 m cannot be hit by anything at all.

remedy.action: Two changes, in this order. (1) Fix the weapon volume rather than compensating for it. At the champion's first active frame the chop's socket capsule spans z = [1.34, 2.57] with the root at z = 0.384, i.e. the blade's near end is 0.95 m in front of its own root and never re-enters the 0.4-1.1 m band. Give the enemy archetypes' `chop_overhead` and `thrust` clip archetypes in game/data/combat/clips.json a low phase — a follow-through that brings the guard socket down through the attacker's own front quarter — so the swept hull covers the band the attacker is walking through. Verify with `--root-dz 0`, which isolates the blade from the corridor. (2) Stop the body corridor paying the weapon's damage. Give `hitgeometry.json §body_hazard` its own `motion_value` and `poise_damage` (a shoulder-check is a shove, not a cut) and resolve it against `struck_part` with that value in game/src/combat/resolve.js step 8b, so a trace reader and a player can tell the two apart. Then re-run the contiguity acceptance: with the weapon volume fixed, the spear's and halberd's dead ring disappears because the blade band now starts inside the corridor's outer edge.

game/src/combat/resolve.js (step 8b — use the body hazard's own damage terms)
game/data/combat/movesets/** (W1-10's spear and halberd R1 clips, whose weapon-only minimum is 1.30 m and 1.35 m)
tools/harness/cmb-reach.mjs (add an --ablate body_hazard mode so the weapon volume can be graded on its own)

gaps.what: Restoring the surface pass on cloned materials put two fragment-shader preambles into one program on actor body materials, and they collide on two identifiers. installSurfaceShader (visual-foundation.js:521, :574) and installWaterline (actor.js:302, :310) each declare `uniform float uWetness` and each declare a local `float esWet`. The program does not link. Measured at HEAD: 124 actor-body materials carry the duplicate declaration, 66 of 124 report program.diagnostics.runnable false with 'uWetness : redefinition' and 'esWet : redefinition', and 0 of 65 equipment/frill controls do either.
gaps.why_it_matters: The player and every NPC in the game are drawn as a floating chest barrel, two detached boots, a pair of horns and their weapon — no head, no arms, no legs — which is the first thing the owner would see on opening the game right now.

remedy.action: PRESERVE the copy seam exactly as built — installCopySeam/adoptMaterialCopy, the JSON recipe in userData, the clone-not-copy choice and the chaining in installWaterline are all correct and are not what is broken. The delta is a rename, in one function. In game/src/render/actor.js#installWaterline (lines 287-327): rename the uniform `uWetness` to `uWaterlineWetness` at its declaration (:302), at the shader.uniforms assignment (:297) and at both uses (:310, :311); rename the local `float esWet` to `esWaterlineWet` at its declaration (:310) and both uses (:313, :319). Prefix `esBand` and `esMeniscus` in the same pass — they are unique today by luck rather than by design, and the next hook added to this chain will collide with them. Do NOT rename anything in installSurfaceShader: it is the shared library and its names are load-bearing for setWorldWetness(). Then add the missing tripwire, which is the durable half of this remedy: a check that no material in the live scene has program.diagnostics.runnable === false, wired into tools/visual/w1-30-surface-orphan-census.mjs so the standing census can see a link failure — its five existing checks structurally cannot, which is why all of them were green over a broken build.
remedy.acceptance: Cheapest gate first, and it already exists and is already red: `node tools/visual/w1-f1-critic-shader-collision.mjs` returns 0 for all four checks, with BODY-PROGRAM-IS-RUNNABLE reporting 0 of at least 100 actor-body programs failing to link and NO-DUPLICATE-UNIFORM-DECLARATION reporting 0 duplicates, while CONTROL-IS-CLEAN and CONTROL-PROGRAM-IS-RUNNABLE stay green. Then, and only then, re-take the frames: re-run `node corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-ORPHANED-SURFACE-SHADERS-CRITIC/base-frame-ab.mjs` against a fresh two-arm capture and require the player's skin and cloth body surfaces to be PRESENT at all 8 orbit angles in BOTH arms, so the shipped-configuration player delta is attributable to shading rather than to geometry appearing. Hard fail: any actor-body material with runnable false. The gap closes when the census itself goes red on a deliberately re-introduced duplicate and green on the shipped tree.

gaps.what: The fix moved the distance term and stopped at the constant floor the distance term was standing on. `game/src/render/water.js:111` still reads `esSurface=mix(esDepth,esReflection,(.25+esGrazing*.50)*uWaterReflectionStrength)`, and line 112 carries 0.68 of that into the frame, so EVERY water pixel at EVERY viewing angle still composites a fixed 0.25 x 0.68 = 17% of the planar/screen reflection target — at normal incidence, where the Fresnel reflectance of water is about 2%. The target is half-resolution (renderer.js:125, verified) and refreshed only when the camera has moved 0.24 m or six simulation frames have passed (renderer.js:1424, verified), so what is composited is a smeared, stale image of the canopy. MEASURED FROM OUTPUT, not argued: with `renderer.quality.waterReflection = false` the reflection accounts for 23.2% of a water pixel's brightness at the deck vista pose on the shipped build (mean |delta| 19.321 over mean base luma 83.199, on 169,177 renderer-derived water-mask pixels), and the same frame with it off is markedly darker and greener and reads closer to RI-WLD10 §8's 'black standing water' for a region the same data file declares at k = 4.5 (0.67 m visibility). AND THE BUILDER'S OWN NUMBERS SAY THIS IS THE REMAINING TERM, not renderer.js. Its fourteen-arm sweep is linear in that mix weight: its two measured points on the pinned tree are (weight 0.610 -> x_rms 7.711) and (weight 0.000 -> x_rms 3.921, the `term-no-reflection` arm), the line through them is x_rms = 3.921 + 6.213w, and it predicts 5.474 at weight 0.250 against the 5.484 the shipped build actually measures — 0.2% error. gaps.what: The level-up screen — which RI-PRG04 §1 makes the hearth's defining affordance and calls 'THE ONLY PLACE LEVELLING IS POSSIBLE' — cannot be opened at any of the 29 shipped sapwells. Measured at hearth-archon, hearth-lilmoth and hearth-gideon: standing on the basin, with the hearth registry itself reporting `standing_at: hearth-<id>` and immediately after a successful `restAt()`, `openMenu('levelup')` is REFUSED 3/3 with "the level-up screen exists at a HEARTH only (RI-UIX03 L1)"; with the harness override `setAtHearth(true)` — which has no in-game counterpart — the same call OPENS 1/1. The gate at game/src/engine.js:2011 is `!!(this.hearths && this.hearths.atHearth && this.hearths.atHearth(this.sim)) || !!this.sim._uiForceHearth`, and HearthSystem (game/src/sim/hearth.js) defines list/get/count/nearest/at/gateAt/menu and no `atHearth`. The first disjunct is `undefined` at every well in the province and the only writer of the second is `__HARNESS.setAtHearth()`. `_spendSouls()` is reachable from exactly one producer (game/src/ui/system.js:322, inside `case 'levelup'`), so souls have no sink anywhere in the running build.
gaps.why_it_matters: The player banks souls, risks them, dies, walks back and recovers exactly 4,200 of them — and then cannot spend one, which makes the entire death economy this piece implements so carefully a loop with nothing at the end of it.

remedy.action: Add the missing predicate to the hearth registry that already answers the question. In game/src/sim/hearth.js, add to HearthSystem: `atHearth(sim) { return !!this.at(sim.player.pos[0], sim.player.pos[2]); }` — `at(x, z)` already exists and already tests each well's own `interact_radius_m`, and `listHearths().standing_at` is built from it, so the registry is right and only the method name the UI calls is missing. Then demote `sim._uiForceHearth` to a declared test override: keep it (arena scenarios need it) but have `setAtHearth()` set a flag that `getUIState()` reports, so a probe that leans on it is visible in its own output. While in this file, note the same shape elsewhere: `game/data/world/respawn.json` names `engine.spawn(id, x, z, {named: true})` as the producer of the six never-respawn flags and `engine.spawn()` copies only `opts.as` and `opts.yaw` — fix that in the same pass (three lines) so the S5 classifier has a world-side writer and is not reachable only through `setEntityNamed()`.

gaps.what: Round 2's build fix guards the COMPLETED calibration by pad id — `const perm = this.calibrationResult && this.calibrationResult.id === st.id ? ... : null` — and I re-derived it: calibrate a stranger through all six prompts, unplug, plug in a standard pad, and index 0 fires `interact` and index 5 fires `light`. Correct. But nothing guards the calibration IN PROGRESS. `this.calibration` is instance state with no pad id on it, `_beginCalibration()` is triggered from `_adoptPad()`, `_dropPad()` never clears it, and it never times out. `poll()` then runs `_calibrationPoll(st)` against whatever pad is currently active. Measured on dcf1d36 with my own driver: answer 2 of 6 prompts on an unrecognised pad, unplug it (n_pads 0) -> `calibrating: true`, prompt still 3/6; plug in a mapping:'standard' pad -> indices 0, 1, 2 and 3 ALL produce NOTHING, a completely dead pad; those four presses are consumed as the stranger's calibration answers and the prompt advances 3/6 -> 5/6; finishing the sequence writes result_id 'Xbox 360 Controller (XInput STANDARD GAMEPAD)' carrying the stranger's permutation, after which index 0 fires `roll`, index 4 `menu` and index 5 `lock_on`; after 600 further frames it is still calibrating.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the same player-visible symptom the round's own commit message claims to have fixed — 'Calibrate one gamepad and the next one you plug in fires the wrong buttons' — reached by an ordinary route instead of an exotic one. The owner plugs a GameSir X2s in its DualSense-like HID mode, the game correctly starts the six-prompt calibration, and the USB-C connector jogs loose. That is not a hypothetical: it is the exact scenario M-P12 was written for and passes on. They re-seat it or reach for a normal pad, and the pad is dead with an in-fiction prompt on screen that never goes away. On a phone, index 0 is the only index there ever is. The round's one build fix and its one repaired instrument were pointed at the same route into the same defect and neither was asked what else could get there — M-P15 only ever calibrates and never disconnects.

remedy.action: game/src/input/gamepad.js, in _dropPad() after `this.pads.delete(idx)`: `if (st && this.calibration && !this.calibration.done) this.calibration = null;` — a calibration belongs to the pad it was begun on, exactly as the completed result now does. I applied this in the page and re-ran the identical sequence: `calibrating: false` after the unplug, and the standard pad's index 0 fires `interact` and index 5 fires `light`. Delete-the-fix reproduces the defect exactly, in both directions.
remedy.acceptance: A --self-test leg that begins a calibration, disconnects the pad mid-sequence, connects a mapping:'standard' pad and asserts index 0 fires `interact` — and that the leg goes red when the one line is removed. Plus M-P15 extended to run its sequence a second time with a disconnect at prompt 3, reporting the action the pad really fired when it is not `interact`, which is the property the repaired M-K18/M-P23 already have.

gaps.what: RI-JRN03's entire 'Discoverability without instruction' block — 14 of its 100 points, and the home of hard fail HF5 — is unmeasured, and the one check in it that reports a result reports it from an empty buffer. M-K20 searches window.__HARNESS.getRenderedText() for instruction tokens and passed with `frames: 0`. I drove the register in seven named states (arena_flat, helstrom-market, thorn-hall, ui-journal, npc_showcase, default, settlement_primary_street) and through uiOpen('dialogue'), uiOpen('menu') and uiOpen('rest'): entries = 0 and summary.surfaces = {} in every single one, while getUIState() at the same instant reports three HUD elements carrying drawn text ('5', 'LIGHT', 'Spark-Dart'). game/src/render/text-register.js instruments only the 'dialogue' and 'title' surfaces and neither ever writes. M-K21 and M-K22 — the other 8 points of the block, M-K22 being the second half of HF5 — do not exist in tools/journey/input-checks.mjs at all; nor do M-K8 (HF3), M-K9 (HF4), M-N1/M-N2/M-N3/M-N5(HF10)/M-N7, M-P14, M-P20, M-P24 (HF7) or M-P25. That is 13 scored ids returning 0 to `grep -c` over the instrument, 28 of RI-JRN03's 100 points and 12 of RI-JRN04's, and five named hard-fail gates that no instrument can fire. The build's `--self-test` takes 5 instruments red — M-P5, M-P3, M-P1, M-P6, M-P17 — and not one of them is a check in this block.
gaps.why_it_matters: The measurement floor is the reason the undrawn touch overlay could ship with 41/41 green, and it is why nobody would be able to tell next round whether the overlay was actually drawn or the same orphan text was moved somewhere else: the only instrument that inspects drawn strings is looking at a buffer nothing writes.

remedy.action: Three steps, in order. (1) MAKE THE REGISTER REAL: game/src/render/text-register.js wraps CanvasRenderingContext2D.fillText but only for the 'dialogue' and 'title' surfaces; route every text-drawing surface through it — HUD, menu, rest, the rebinding screen, and the touch/rotate surfaces once they are drawn — so getRenderedText() returns what is on the glass. (2) GIVE M-K20 A POSITIVE CONTROL IN --self-test: add a leg that draws a known token ('Press E') on a non-settings surface and asserts M-K20 goes red; a leg that asserts the token is NOT found when drawn on the settings surface; and make the check itself report `unmeasurable` rather than `pass` whenever entries === 0, so an empty stream can never again read as a clean bill of health. (3) IMPLEMENT THE MISSING IDS: M-K8, M-K9, M-K21, M-K22, M-P14, M-P20, M-P24 and M-P25 as instrument checks in tools/journey/input-checks.mjs, each with a --self-test perturbation leg; and run the Naive pass (M-N1/N2/N3/N5/N7 for RI-JRN03, M-N1/N3/N5 for RI-JRN04) as the separate fresh-agent protocol its own section specifies, since it is a procedure and not an instrument.

gaps.what: Walking through a door sets sim.env.interior and moves the body to the declared interior spawn, and does not change what is drawn: renderer.setCell() has exactly one caller, Engine._applyCell(), and _applyCell() is called from loadState, the census staging, the barge reset and the save-load path but never from useDoor() or leaveInterior(). Measured over the WHOLE population: all 115 interiors entered through enterInterior() from a province start — 115 of 115 entered, 0 refused, 0 errors — and 0 of 115 changed the drawn cell; the visible set reads ['province'] after every door. In detail, after enterInterior('thorn-hall'), across six fixed steps and an explicit renderFrame(), the visible cell set is still ['province'] while cellFor(env) reads 'interior'; calling _applyCell() by hand switches it to ['interior'] (the control arm). After exitInterior the visible cell is still ['interior'] while the body stands outdoors in Thorn. And there would be almost nothing to draw if it did switch: cellFor() maps five interiors to hand-built W1-07 rooms and returns the generic 'interior' cell — scene.js buildHall(), 249 triangles, one light — for the other 113 of 115, while interior.props (18 on a typical shop), .lights (10), .containers and .unique_item have zero consumers anywhere in game/src.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the same defect the piece itself found and fixed one layer down. sim.player.pos turned out to be a mirror that combat-bridge.mirror() overwrote, so a door taken on frame N was undone on frame N+1, and in the builder's own words nothing was red because 'sim.env.interior was set correctly the whole time — every census-shaped check passed while the player never actually went anywhere.' The body half was fixed and the render half was not, and tools/world/w1-04-consumption.mjs cannot see it because it never reads the renderer: all thirteen of its checks would still pass on a build where no door has ever shown anyone a room. ARBITRATION §3 settles what that is worth — 'a model with no demonstrated consumer is unmeasurable => 0, exactly as a missing model is; from the player's chair they are the same thing.' From the player's chair, 115 named interiors, 202 buildings, eight architecture kits and 260 people who live in rooms are one hall you cannot get into. RI-WLD13 §2 named this exact failure before the piece began: 'the difference between a settlement of buildings and a settlement of building-shaped doors.'

remedy.action: Two changes, in this order. gaps.what: All 43 martial texts carry the same three orthographic and page-furniture fingerprints, every one of them in a place tools/check-prose.mjs does not read. Bare Arabic numerals run 128.5 per 10k words against Morrowind's measured 9.3 (13.8x) and against the rest of this project's own library at 24.9; 65.1% of the texts carry two or more ALL-CAPS section headings against Morrowind's 2.1% (31x) and this library's 8.4%; and 60 of the 188 headings carry a ', WHICH ...' appositive against 1 in Morrowind's whole 241-book corpus. Two of the three are gate artifacts: check-prose RULE-06 penalises SPELLED counts four..twenty, so de-spelling turns the row green (the status file banks it as a win, 90.77 -> 52.42), and RULE-17/RULE-28's ', which is' tic did not go away in round 4 — it moved one line up into the headings, where a sentence-level detector cannot see it.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player who reads three of these books in three different towns is meant to meet three people and instead meets one writer in three costumes — and the seam shows inside single sentences, as in 'Every file is to carry 2 bills and they are to be given to the two largest men in it' and 'Water bottle, 2 — two, not one'.

remedy.action: Three mechanical edits, none of which rewrites an argument, an image or a joke. (1) Re-spell numerals in narrative prose across the 43 texts, keeping Arabic figures ONLY where a document would really carry them — the muster leaf, the rack tally, the day-book, the handbill's stoppages, registry numbers and 3E dates. This will re-redden check-prose RULE-06, and that is the correct outcome: the rule's own reference is Morrowind and Morrowind spells them, so re-baseline RULE-06 against tools/uesp/mw-book-stats.py's measured distribution (one 68.0% decaying smoothly to thirteen 2.9%, no bump) instead of a flat penalty. (2) Break the heading template: take texts carrying two or more ALL-CAPS headings from 65% to at most 20%, delete the ', WHICH ...' appositive from at least 45 of the 60 headings, and leave at most 12 headings beginning with WHAT — several of these texts should carry no headings at all, since a hunter's oral teaching, a nephew's account of two uncles arguing and a letter found folded in a helmet do not come with a table of contents. (3) Convert Imperial-year counts to sap-falls in at least 8 of the 15 Argonian-authored texts and let at least one refuse to convert, the way game/data/books/quest-keys.json already does. Separately, extend tools/check-prose.mjs to read headings: it reads sentences only, which is why 60 instances of a tracked tic survived a round whose entire subject was tics.

gaps.what: 37,819 words in 65 texts open 65/65 in the engine across 324 pages, and the only thing a player can do with any of it is read it. Both mechanical consumers the two items name are dead code. (1) `book.knowledge_key` is read by no file in game/src/; the three non-violent quest resolutions that gate on those keys — Q-SOUL-02 res_seal, Q-LILM-01 res_rootkeepers, Q-DEEP-01 res_broker — are unreachable by any route in the shipped build, and the engine reports the identical refusal before and after the book has been opened and read to the last page. (2) `book.topics_taught` (60 books, 116 topics) is read by nothing; opening all 60 in the engine leaves topicsKnown empty. That field is RI-UIX05 R3's permitted exception and the item's entire declared AR-3 seam crossing.
gaps.why_it_matters: RI-UIX05 §D's last row exists, in the item's own words, because 'a player who read the right book three regions ago knows a name, and a name is a parley key (S13) or a topic (R3's exception) ... this row owns whether the reading surface is connected to anything.' It reports 17 by reading JSON and 0 by asking the game. Three of the build's non-violent exits are closed, which pushes against the >=45% non-combat resolution bar; and the piece's only route across the Souls/Morrowind seam does not exist. ARBITRATION §3 CONSUMPTION is explicit that a model with no demonstrated consumer scores 0 exactly as a missing model does, because from the player's chair they are the same thing.

steps: In game/src/ui/system.js, in the open('book', {id}) branch that already resolves the book record (around line 129), on FIRST open of a given book id call a new questEngine.readBook(bookRecord).

readBook(): for each t in book.topics_taught, append through game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js's fold-safe appender into sim.quest.topicsKnown — that module exists and is already the correct door, and it dedupes on the folded key.

gaps.what: Three of nineteen registered contradiction pairs have both sides reachable by a player. Fifteen have neither side reachable anywhere under game/. The ford pair — the best writing in the project — and the province's central moral fact (CF-062/CF-D008, whether subjects of the Empire are held as property, argued by the-blessings-of-the-coast against ledger-and-journal-of-andrel-vorin) are each argued by two books that are referenced nowhere in the world.
gaps.why_it_matters: The bar for this piece was that the library is books, not a codex, and that two books which disagree are the point. The disagreement was authored, registered, sealed and gated — and then left where nothing can reach it. This is the project's eighteen-plus pattern in its most painful form: not a model nothing reads, but a model that IS read, wired to a corpus the reader cannot get to. The three pairs that do survive are all the same argument, about one document, in one building, so the surviving diversity is near zero. RI-LOR06's discipline passes and the player still cannot perceive the province disagreeing with itself about the Hist, the Flu, the xanmeers, or slavery.

gaps.what: This piece's headline artifact is a three-arm experiment showing the shipped panner at r = 0.9999 and the rule it replaced at r = −0.5207 on the same fixture, and it concludes `detector_goes_red = true`. The −0.5207 is a property of that fixture, not of the rule. Under the legacy rule a blow the player lands is positioned at the attacker, so dx = dz = 0 and pan = sin(atan2(0,0) − playerYaw) = sin(−playerYaw): the target's position is NEVER READ, and the correlation with the target's true bearing is therefore whatever the fixture's player-yaw history happens to make it. Sweeping the fixture on the shipped code at HEAD 5c4c5b0, the same broken rule scores r = −0.0759 (orbit anchored to player facing), +0.7768 (orbit anchored to world — within 0.03 of the bar), +0.6034 (stationary target, player free to turn), null (still target), and +1.0000 with 100 impacts, 99 distinct pan values and a 70° bearing spread on 'stationary enemy, player turning on the spot'. On that last fixture the BROKEN rule PASSES M6 outright and the shipped `detector_goes_red` predicate reports green. That fixture is not exotic: it is a player circling a standing enemy, which is what M6's own method text ('correlate audioLog.pan against the enemy's bearing from the player') invites a critic to build. The invariant that does discriminate is already in every log row and is not in the pass condition: distance_m_max is 0.0000 on all five legacy arms and 1.13–1.45 m on all five shipped arms.
gaps.why_it_matters: The shipped panner is correct — that is not in dispute and the fix was a real one. What is broken is the thing that certifies it. A check that reports green on the exact anti-pattern the piece exists to have removed is worse than no check, because the next critic will run M6 the obvious way, get r ≈ 1.0, and bank a regression as a pass. RI-AUD02 S6 explicitly delegates its own non-self-report backstop to this measurement ('the camera-orbit pan measurement, which cannot be self-reported wrongly'), so two items rest on it. And the shipped sabotage switch — setAudioPanSource('attacker'), the mechanism that exists so a build cannot run the defect quietly — is only as good as the predicate reading it. AGENT-PROTOCOL rule 4: a probe that cannot fail is worse than no probe, and this one cannot fail on a fixture a reasonable person would choose.

remedy.action: Make M6's pass condition test the property that is actually invariant, and make the fixture sweep part of the check rather than a single hand-picked orbit. Concretely: (1) add `distance_m` to the P4 pass condition — a player-landed impact must report a non-zero distance to the listener, and the legacy rule cannot satisfy that on any fixture; (2) run P4 over at least the 'stationary target, player turning' fixture in addition to the orbit, and require the shipped rule to pass ALL of them and the sabotaged rule to fail ALL of them, rather than requiring one arm to go red; (3) fold tools/audio/critic-m6-fixture-sweep.mjs (or its logic) into tools/audio/impact-browser.mjs so the sweep runs where the real WebAudio panner does. The tool already exits 3 when it finds a fixture on which the broken rule passes, so it is its own regression test.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/audio/critic-m6-fixture-sweep.mjs exits 0 with finding 'LEGACY_NEVER_PASSES' — i.e. no fixture in the sweep passes the acceptance criterion under panSource='attacker' — while the shipped rule passes every fixture in the sweep; and impact-browser.mjs P4 reports the same across at least two fixture geometries.

gaps.what: The effect catalogue is a complete, correctly priced, deterministic parameter space with one behaviour behind it. Measured across all 71 shipped spells: 5 of 55 effects produce the mechanical consequence their own record describes (fire, frost, shock and poison damage, and damage_health); 1 is partial (levitate meters altitude and charges 1.5 Focus/m but never moves pos[1]); 16 resolve only as HP damage equal to their own magnitude — demoralise deals 111 hp and the enemy stays AGGRO, calm_beast deals 31 hp and the beast stays in COMBAT, open_lock deals 31 hp to a creature, charm 184, corrode 310, lock_lock 184, silence 31, paralyse 12 with no buildup field on the enemy record at all; and 33 are a row in effects_active that no other system in the build reads — shield and resist_element each mitigate 0 of a scripted 100-damage hit, the_greater_mending heals 0 with the player at 420 of 620, feather leaves equip_load_pct at 24 and roll_class at LIGHT, fortify_skill satisfies no gate, bind_lesser summons nothing (entity count 0 to 0), wall creates no collider, leap adds 0 m of altitude, recall completes its 210-frame ritual and leaves the player at exactly the coordinates it started from, hist_sight completes and writes 0 journal entries, and all five Veiling effects leave getStealthState() byte-identical to baseline against the stealth system shipping in the same build.
gaps.why_it_matters: S19 says spell effects are tools and quests must be solvable with them, so a player who buys the Open spell to get past the warded door in The Warded Ledger will instead do thirty-one points of damage to the door's guard, and the >=45% non-combat resolution bar that magic is supposed to supply a fifth of is satisfied only in JSON.

remedy.action: Replace the single generic applicator with a per-effect handler registry. Concretely: (1) In game/src/sim/combat-bridge.js, the spell-contact callback currently accumulates `dmg += outputOf(effect, magnitude)` for every effect whose utility_class is null OR whose geometry is not 'none' — restrict that accumulation to the five damage effects (fire_damage, frost_damage, shock_damage, poison_damage, damage_health) plus the status buildup each declares, so a non-damage effect can never deal HP damage. (2) Add game/src/sim/magic/apply.js: a table keyed by effect id, one handler per effect, called from MagicSystem.applyEffects(), each handler writing into the system RI-MAG06 §B names for that effect. (3) Wire the eight consumers that already exist in this build before touching anything that does not: CombatBody.equipLoadPct/tier for feather and burden (RI-CMB01's 30.00/70.00 cliff must stay exactly where it is); CombatBody.hp for restore_health, drain_health and absorb_health, and hpMax for drain; a mitigation multiplier ahead of the damage write for shield, resist_element and sap_ward; sim.stealth.d.detection's V terms and sound radius for chameleon (clamped 80), invisibility (breaking on attack, cast, interact, container and COMBAT), muffle, night_eye and false_face; the S11 buildup meter for paralyse, so it crosses a threshold instead of arriving in one frame; enemy alert_state and the leash for calm_beast, demoralise and frenzy, ending COMBAT with zero death events; CombatBody.pos for mark/recall/intervention, so a completed ritual actually moves the player; and a real locomotion mode for levitate that writes pos[1], caps horizontal speed at 1.4 m/s and drops light, heavy, block, roll and parry. (4) Every effect whose consuming system genuinely does not exist yet (water bands, the lock register, item condition, the quest knowledge store) gets an explicit UNMEASURABLE row in the census naming the piece that owns it, capped at five per RI-MAG06 M6.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run RI-MAG06's census (reference implementation at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-14/consolidate.mjs). EFFECT-FUNCTION >= 50/55; HP_DAMAGE_ONLY == 0 (hard fail above 3); UNREAD_TIMER <= 2; UNMEASURABLE <= 5, each naming its owning piece. Plus these five named single-trace assertions, each of which fails today: still_the_beast on an aggroed beast_slitherfang ends COMBAT with alert_state != AGGRO and zero death events; feather moves roll_class across RI-CMB01's 30.00% cliff with the discontinuity still at exactly 30.00; thick_skin reduces a scripted 100-damage hit by the declared fraction; the_deep_chameleon changes getStealthState().V; recall moves getPlayerStats().pos to the mark.

gaps.what: MagicSystem.skills is a private object initialised to {sorcery:30, root_speech:30, warding:30, veiling:30} that no gameplay path writes. Measured in four shipped states (default, arena_flat, dungeon_primary, helstrom-market): 47 of 72 shipped spells attunable and 25 refused — all 17 tier-3 and all 8 tier-4 — and setAttuned() drops them silently. 40 casts at a live target, a HEARTH rest, H.setSkills() on the character sheet and H.grantSkillUse('cast_effective') all leave the tier-3 attune at 0/1 and quoteSpell().attunable_now false; only H.setMagicSkills(), a harness call with no in-game counterpart, flips it to 1/1 and true. Spellmaking is capped at two effects for the whole game ('3 effects needs skill 50; your best relevant school is 30'). In the other direction, RI-MAG04's magic resolutions gate on sim.progression.skills, which is {} in every shipped state and which the magic system never writes: the coupling between the character's magic skill and the magic system is 0.00 in both directions, with the null control clean (perturbing magic.skills 30->100 does flip the gate, so the probe is driving a live gate and not a stub).
gaps.why_it_matters: A mage who plays this game for forty hours casts exactly the spells they could cast in the first minute — a third of the shipped catalogue, every tier-3 and tier-4 spell, and every three-effect spell they might commission are locked behind a number that nothing they do can move, and the quest resolutions magic exists to unlock read a different, empty number.

remedy.action: Make MagicSystem.skills a VIEW of sim.progression.skills rather than a private copy: replace the literal at game/src/sim/magic/system.js:59 with a getter that reads sim.progression.skills (mapping root_speech <-> root-speech, which are spelled differently in the two files today), so _effectiveSkillFor, focusCost, the tier gate and quoteSpell's effect-count all read the character sheet. Then close the loop that fills the sheet: add `skill` to the effect_apply and spell_hit event payloads in game/src/sim/magic/system.js and game/src/sim/combat-bridge.js so game/src/character/skilluse.js:stepSkillUse banks the SPELL'S OWN school instead of hardcoding 'sorcery'; and make setAttuned() emit an `attune_refused` event with the shortfall instead of silently returning a shorter list. Ensure sim.progression.skills is non-empty in the shipped states (engine.js:575 fills it from ch.skills, which is empty when no character has been composed) — coordinate with W1-07, whose census owns that seeding, and record the seam if it cannot be done here.

gaps.what: The spell-making and enchanting systems — the entire Morrowind half of this piece and the reason RI-MAG03 exists — are reachable only from window.__HARNESS. `makeSpell` has exactly one caller in the whole build and it is the test harness; so does `enchantQuote`. The eight menus a player can open are inventory, journal, book, levelup, sheet, spells, container and map, and `spells` is a list of what is already attuned. No NPC in game/data/npcs/** offers a spellmaking or enchanting service; the shipped service vocabulary has 17 values and neither word is among them; no dialogue topic mentions either. game/data/magic/enchanting.json names seven enchanters and spellwrights with settlements attached — journeyman_lilmoth, journeyman_gideon, journeyman_stormhold, journeyman_helstrom, master_blackrose, master_soulrest, recluse_stone_wastes — and its own note reads 'Four in the world, and walking to one is part of the cost (RI-MAG03 §A, S7)'. None of the seven exists as a person anywhere in the world; their ids appear in exactly one other file, enchant-services.json, as a foreign key to nobody.
gaps.why_it_matters: ARBITRATION §3's CONSUMPTION clause governs: a model with no demonstrated world-side consumer is unmeasurable and therefore 0, 'exactly as a missing model is — from the player's chair they are the same thing.' RI-MAG03's own bar is blunter: a critic must be able to build, buy and cast a spell that appears nowhere in spells.json, and the moment that matters is walking into the guild and constructing an object that has never existed before. There is nowhere to walk to. Every one of the 97 dials this round spent itself measuring exists so that a player can turn it, and the player has no hands on any of them. Shipped in this state the game has a fixed list of 72 spells — which is precisely the failure the doctrine names: a fixed list of abilities with good frame data is a failure of this piece however well it fights. It is also the cheapest blocking gap on the list, because the arithmetic, the four gates, the clamps, the tier ladder, the commission price, the save round-trip and the refusal prose all exist and all work. What is missing is a person to talk to and a screen to talk on.
