gaps.what: Moving `map` to second in `UISystem.WALK_ORDER` put it immediately before `journal`, and `map`'s own navigable ring excludes `journal` (NEVER_ADJACENT, enforcing RI-UIX04 Q7). The forward page-walk from the inventory therefore steps over the journal and never returns: inventory -> map -> sheet -> spells -> wait -> (closes). Before the fix the same walk visited all five peer screens and reached the journal on the first press. The journal now costs three page-turns WITH a direction reversal on desktop and eight taps with a reversal on a phone, and swap_left from the inventory closes the menu rather than paging backwards, so the reversal is not something a player discovers by accident. The map went from four presses to one; the journal went from one press to off the forward walk entirely.
gaps.why_it_matters: The quest log is the screen a Morrowind player opens most, and a player who has found the page-turn control can now press it forever without ever seeing their journal.

remedy.action: Separate `map` and `journal` by at least one screen in `UISystem.WALK_ORDER`, keeping `map` second. `['world', 'inventory', 'map', 'sheet', 'journal', 'spells', 'wait', 'levelup']` is measured and works: the forward walk becomes inventory -> map -> sheet -> journal -> spells -> wait, the map stays one page-turn from the screen `menu` opens, and nothing is skipped. The constraint is structural rather than cosmetic and belongs in a comment beside the constant: any two screens in NEVER_ADJACENT must not be neighbours in WALK_ORDER, because the ring is filtered per-mode and an excluded neighbour is stepped over rather than stopped at. Add the assertion to tools/harness/map-probe.mjs so a future reorder fails a check instead of a player.

gaps.what: Discovery.restore() computes a seven-field audit of the loaded footprint against the blob's own claims — dropped, phantom_cells, missing_cells, claimed_places, derived_places, stood_cells, legacy — and every published surface throws it away: save/state.js:676 keeps only .dropped and mapState() publishes only dropped_on_load. ARBITRATION S38 clause (d) makes 'a discrepancy between the blob's claims and the derivation is ITEMISED, not swallowed' a hard fail, and the S38 gate's own assertion for it (S38-4) cannot see this gap, because S38-4 forges the CLAIM FIELDS — an all-ones raster and all 42 names — and so always produces an itemisation to read. The forgery a forger would actually write supplies no claims at all: with cells:"" and places:[] the two fields S38-4 reads are both ZERO on a save that fills the entire province, while missing_cells reads 42,846 and derived_places reads 42.
gaps.why_it_matters: S38 deliberately gave up tamper-resistance and kept, in exchange, the promise that a save whose claims disagree with its own derivation is itemised rather than swallowed. That promise is currently unkeepable by any instrument: the signal exists for one function call and then goes out of scope. It is also round 1's remedy 1, unactioned, and it is the difference between a build that can report on its own loads and one that cannot. The second-order cost is worse: the new gate reads green on the clause, so the gap is now covered by a passing check.

gaps.what: Across five blind pairs, four of five judges described our surfaces as flat untextured fills with no albedo/normal/roughness response — three of them named it as the single biggest gap, all three at CONFIDENCE: high. In the judges' own words: 'every surface reads as flat diffuse albedo with no specular, roughness variation, or normal-mapped relief, so thatch, plaster, stone and grass all respond to light identically'. The mechanical corroboration is independent of the judges: image-leakcheck's local_contrast_med statistic names the reference on 5 of 5 pairs.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player looking at any surface in the world — masonry, thatch, ground, foliage — sees the same material, because every material is the same material under light; nothing in the build reads as made of anything.

remedy.action: Author and bind a real PBR material set — albedo + normal + roughness/metalness — to the terrain, architecture and foliage materials, so different surfaces produce different specular and micro-shading response under the same light. This is R1 of the ranked, buildable remedy list in corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1.md §3; R2 (contact shadows + AO), R3 (ambient/GI fill with tone-mapped shadow lift) and R4 (ground-plane dressing) follow it there with their own acceptance criteria, and R5 (depth of field) is listed there explicitly TO BE STRUCK because the only evidence for it was manufactured by the pair02/pair03 bokeh confound.
remedy.acceptance: Two named materials in a single capture from the fixed eight slots produce measurably different specular response under the same light; and a wave-2 Protocol A re-run (counterbalanced sides, clean judge context, pair02/pair03 rebuilt against an in-focus plate) returns 'everything responds to light identically' as no pair's SINGLE BIGGEST GAP.

gaps.what: Engine.applySave() and Engine.loadState() both call PopulationSystem.reset(), which sets all 144 posts back to DORMANT, while SoulsSystem.reset() empties the eid ledger the S5 epoch gate is keyed on and death.ordinaryRespawnEpoch never moves. Measured at aaa2f1f on pop-0001, with no hearth rest and no harness respawn verb anywhere: L1 kill 2 bodies -> +98 souls; L2 CONTROL walk out past release_radius_m and back -> post stays CLEARED, 0 bodies, delta 0 (correctly refused); L3 saveState -> loadState -> the post re-materialises with 2 bodies -> kill again -> +98 souls with the epoch unmoved at 0. Repeatable without bound.
gaps.why_it_matters: ARBITRATION S5 and RI-PRG06 §4 both price a respawn at a rest, and the rest is what makes the world clock cost something. This removes the price. RI-PRG06 exists because 'a soul curve without a soul supply is unfalsifiable', and an unbounded farm makes the supply unfalsifiable again; its own 'How we lose' says 'every number in this file is instantly fiction', and RI-AI05 M6 fails at a farm rate >= 3x the clear rate. It also defeats a fix a neighbouring piece built SPECIFICALLY in response to this one: SoulsSystem's header names W1-POPULATION as the reason the boolean re-arm became an epoch gate, and the gate holds against the door that piece anticipated (the walk, proved by the builder's A8 and reproduced as my L2 control) and not against the one this piece opened. The population.reset() call is this piece's line, added by this piece, with its justification written on it: 'which ordinary mobs are dead is exactly what S5 says a rest restores anyway.' S5 says a REST restores them; a load is not a rest.

remedy.action: On applySave, restore each post's CLEARED/DORMANT state from the save instead of resetting all 144 posts to DORMANT — which is also what a player expects, since a reloaded save should not hand back a province they had already cleared. gaps.what: The urgent tile-build branch in Engine._streamProvince() is exempt from the one-unit-of-work-per-step budget AND is evaluated BEFORE it, so any frame on which the body ARRIVES somewhere - a respawn, a teleport, a future fast-travel or cutscene relocation - pays a ~30-tile release plus updateSkin (15,625 vertices) plus updateCover plus updateNear plus two full _buildTile calls in one fixed step.
gaps.why_it_matters: Measured on a real death in the province, the six frames after the respawn cost 337.01, 405.43, 483.96, 361.98, 222.64 and 472.46 ms - about 2,283 ms in total, against the builder's walking worst case of 133.8 ms. FixedLoop.MAX_CATCHUP is 5, so in mode 'play' the accumulator advances at most 83 ms of world and drops the remaining ~2.2 s into catchupDroppedMs. The world stops for two seconds at the exact moment a Souls player has just died and is looking for their bloodstain, which is the most latency-sensitive moment in the game outside a boss swing. The builder never saw it because every one of its runs was a walk, and a walk never enters this branch.

remedy.action: Make the urgent budget respect the work the frame has already done, and declare the arrival as a load boundary.
targets: game/src/engine.js _streamProvince(): move `if (discWork) return;` ABOVE the urgent branch, or change pump(STREAM_URGENT_TILES) to pump(discWork ? 1 : STREAM_URGENT_TILES). The tile under the body is queue[0] with d === 0 and one pump(1) places it; the other eight tiles of the 3x3 are 150-450 m away and can wait a frame each.
game/src/engine.js teleport() and the respawn path: wrap in _boundaryBegin('province_stream') / _boundaryEnd, per RI-PLT03 §B. A boundary you announce is not a hitch.

game/src/engine.js: skip the request() refocus while combat.player.state is inside ATK_* or ROLL_*, letting s.since keep counting. This is the AR-1 remedy and it is far cheaper than making updateSkin fast: a roll covers ~5 m against SKIN_REBUILD_M = 11, so nothing visible moves.

game/src/engine.js STREAM_REFOCUS_M and the disc rebuild distances: budget by METRES SINCE THE LAST REBUILD rather than by frames, so travelRide at 40 m/s gets the throughput it needs instead of a walk's.

gaps.what: The build's rendered-text accessor — `__HARNESS.getRenderedText()`, fed by render/text-register.js — is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of seeing the one surface RI-JRN01 M9 and M15 are aimed at, and the build's own report records a pass over an empty set as a result. render/render.js:90 carries the comment 'Every 2D surface this renderer owns is registered against the one rendered-text register' and then instruments two of three: `this.ui` as 'dialogue' and `this.title` as 'title'. The third, `this.menus = new UISurface(...)` at renderer.js:86, is W1-21's HUD and menus — which is precisely M9's domain, 'every string rendered OUTSIDE a dialogue/journal/book surface'. FALSIFIED, not inferred: I instrumented the menus context at runtime through the register's OWN public instrument() and forced a repaint, and got ZERO entries. Then, in the same freshly-instrumented context, I drew one sentinel through ui/glyphs.js drawText() — the path every string in that surface takes — and one through ctx.fillText(). The register saw the fillText sentinel (1 row) and did not see the glyphs sentinel (0 rows). glyphs.js renders every glyph as a stroked Path (moveTo / lineTo / quadraticCurveTo / stroke) and never calls fillText or strokeText, which the register wraps. So the hole cannot be closed by calling instrument() — the register is blind to that surface by construction. Enumerated directly through UISurface.elements[].text, the opening draws five strings the accessor cannot see: '5', '0', 'LIGHT', 'Spark-Dart' and 'Take A tithe-gourd, empty'. reports/journeys/w1-26-opening.json records `m9.surfaces_searched: 'title (the only non-dialogue drawn surface in the build)'` — which is false — with `distinct_searched: 0` and `hits: []`, and the piece reports M9 as scoreable for the first time on that basis.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is not a missing feature; it is a wrong number that looks right, on the piece's own declared path, in the instrument the whole area was gated on. RI-JRN01 §0.1(a) exists because a canvas-only build returned an empty accessibility tree to the obvious accessor, so a grep over an empty set returned zero hits and read as a clean pass; the amendment's fix was to demand a NAMED accessor demonstrated non-empty. This build supplied one, demonstrated it non-empty ON A DIFFERENT SURFACE, and bought exactly the same false pass one layer down. That is RI-JRN01 How-we-lose #15 reproduced by the fix written to close it — and it is strictly worse than the failure it replaced, because the empty accessibility tree announced its own emptiness while `getRenderedText()` returns twelve confident strings and a summary block. Every future critic of this journey will read it and believe it. The concrete cost this round: M9 (10 points) and M15 (3 points) score 0 of RI-JRN01's 20-point Restraint block; the check that was meant to catch instruction text did not catch the instruction text that is there; and AR-2 fails on a string the build's own sweep reported as absent. The cost next round is larger and less visible — the accessor is now the corpus's only answer to 'what does the frame say?', and it answers for two thirds of the frame.

remedy.action: Make the register see the third surface, then re-run M9 and M15 over it. Two routes, either acceptable. (a) Give ui/glyphs.js drawText() a register call of its own: it already holds the string, x, y, the face and the size at the top of the function, so one `textRegister.note(ctx, s, x, y, size)` before the glyph loop puts it in the same register with the same clip shadow. (b) Have UISurface.el() route every record carrying `text` through a shim that the register wraps, so the tag stays on the element rather than being inferred. Route (a) is smaller and catches anything that draws glyphs, including surfaces nobody has written yet; route (b) is safer against a future surface that draws text some third way. Whichever is taken, `getRenderedText()` must stop advertising `surfaces_instrumented` as a static array and derive it from the contexts actually wrapped, and tools/harness/w1-26-opening.mjs must FAIL rather than pass when its M9 grep searches zero strings — a probe that cannot go red is worse than no probe. Separately, remove or rewrite the interact prompt so it names the object without commanding the player ('A tithe-gourd, empty' rather than 'Take A tithe-gourd, empty').
remedy.acceptance: On a frame of the opening where UISurface.elements[].text is non-empty, `__HARNESS.getRenderedText({notSurface:['dialogue']})` returns a distinct set that CONTAINS every one of those strings (set equality, not merely non-empty), and the register reports them with a clip flag. Then M9's grep over that set returns 0 hits and M15's returns 0 hits, and tools/harness/w1-26-opening.mjs exits non-zero if `m9.distinct_searched === 0`. Falsification required in the same run: draw a sentinel through ui/glyphs.js drawText() and assert the register sees it, exactly as this verdict's probe asserts it currently does not.

gaps.what: The road/settlement join is a BUILD-TIME consumption with no gate. game/data/world/roads.json carries the answer; planSettlement() produces the question; nothing re-asks it and nothing notices when it changes. The check that would notice exists, is offline, runs in under a second, already exits non-zero on failure, and is run by nothing. The join went stale twenty-four minutes after it was cut and has been stale for every commit since.
gaps.why_it_matters: The province is not crossable on foot by a body with a collision capsule while a house stands on the trunk road — which is the exact defect this piece was dispatched to remove, and §P.4 of the dispatch was retracted because of it. It is also the shape the project keeps losing to: a correct model, correctly instrumented, whose consumer silently stopped agreeing with it. Here the consumer did not stop reading; the thing it reads moved. Sixteen subsystems have shipped a model nothing reads. This is the seventeenth failure mode: a model something read ONCE.

remedy.action: Four steps, in order. (1) Run `node tools/world/build-roads.mjs` and commit game/data/world/roads.json — verified on a scratch copy of the tree exactly as it stands (R-REMEDY in reports/critic-road-join/consume.json). (2) Add `node tools/world/road-through-building.mjs` to the gate set by editing the SOURCE LIST the INDEX.md gate table is generated from, not the table. (3) Change road-through-building.mjs to plan with the interiors — planSettlement(doc, interiors), or the union of that and planSettlement(doc, {}) — so the gate asks the game's question rather than the check's; at HEAD the difference is 6 blocked samples and one whole building (blackrose-house-1). (4) Replace road-through-building.mjs --self-test's hard-coded stormhold-scribe subject with a run-time search over every building x every leg point for the nearest (building, road point) pair, perturb THAT through the same path the game uses, and require flag / restore-to-baseline; tools/world/critic-road-join-ingame.mjs --self-test is a working implementation of exactly this.

gaps.what: The gold a player can actually spend is held in `combat.world.gold` (rebuilt by `Engine._buildCombat`) and `sim.stealth.p.gold`, and neither is ever written back into `sim.progression.gold` — the only gold register the save carries. On 3 of the 38 shipped named states (helstrom-market, rootlands-well-graph, stormhold-street) a plain save/load destroys 600 gold, on 10 of 10 seeds, and it survives a real cold reload through IndexedDB as well. Every shipped instrument reports clean while it happens: M1 hash equal, M2 diff empty, M4 set difference empty both ways, `getDurableFieldCensus().ok` true, and the M5 trace byte-identical. Falsified with the null control — blanking `progression.gold` and `fight.loadout.gold` out of the blob produces exactly the same world as leaving them alone, which is CONSUMPTION coupling 0 on a field this very repair added to the manifest.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player who walks into Helstrom market with 600 gold, saves, and comes back a week later has been robbed of it, and the bribe that ARBITRATION §1 guarantees as a non-lethal exit from a fight is refused for want of money they still believe they have.

remedy.action: Make one register the authority for the purse and give the save that register, then widen the census so the class of defect cannot recur. (a) In `game/src/engine.js`, have `setGold`, `combat/parley.js applyAccept` (`world.gold -= spent`), `travelRide` (`world.gold -= fare`), `fenceSell`/`bribeWitness` (`stealth.p.gold`) and the capture path all write through to `sim.progression.gold`, and have `_buildCombat` read only from it — or, if the three registers must stay, serialise `combat.world.gold` and `sim.stealth.p.gold` as their own manifest paths under Progression with the same rebase discipline the rest of the group uses. (b) Extend `Engine.getDurableFieldCensus()`'s `shot()` to clone `this.combat.world`, `this.travel`, `this.crime`/`sim.stealth`, `this.conversation` and `sim._traversal` — it currently walks a declared subset and its own comment warns that 'a census that walks a subset of the simulation is an instrument that certifies a subset'. (c) Add a save point with money in it to `tools/journey/state-diff.mjs`'s pre-roll, so the sweep can fail.

gaps.why_it_matters: This piece exists to make theft have geography and memory — witnesses who saw you, guards who know things, factions who care, consequences that persist. All of that is built, correct and measured, and every gram of it is discharged at the point of sale by a fence who will buy you your victim's own furniture at the honest-goods price, in the victim's own town, while the fence three towns away pays more. From the player's chair, stealing has no map: it is strictly optimal to rob the house next door and sell to the man who drinks with the owner, and the refusal lines somebody wrote for exactly that moment — 'That belongs to Ahnassi Dark-Water of terraces. gaps.what: RI-CHR01 §4 states the questionnaire's purpose in its own words — the Warden-Scribe says the profession aloud, 'which is the moment the route is for' — and RI-JRN09 M3 requires that line on the frame in 100% of named runs. Measured at the node the line is spoken (writ.birthsign, its only opportunity, because `spoken` carries only the reply to the last answer): 0 of 12 named runs across six races and two upbringings. The mechanism is ui.js's overflow-sacrifice loop — `while (contentH > maxH && spokenLines.length) spokenLines.shift()` — which drops the scribe's previous reply from the front until the panel fits its 48%-of-frame-height budget, and at the birthsign node (nine options plus a two-line naming sentence) the naming line is always what goes. The builder's own instrument reports 100% because it does not test that line: jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 runs `blob.indexOf(norm(c.class_name)) >= 0` over the concatenated drawn text of every node in the walk, and the same round added 'Trade declared: %ClassName' to the writ's drawn identity block at writ.stamp, so the class name is on the frame whatever the scribe did or did not say. Measured side by side on the same twelve runs: the naming LINE 0 of 12; the class NAME substring 12 of 12. The same mechanism eats the upbringing reply ('The interior. I will write the marsh. There are people here who will read that and stand up straighter, and people who will read it and count their doors.') and the birthsign reply ('The tide was in and the root had more than it needed. It gave you a swallow it did not owe you.'), which is why AC = 6 of 7 is evidenced entirely by fields of one printed form.
gaps.why_it_matters: Morrowind's opening is remembered because a bored functionary looks at your answers and tells you what you apparently are. This build computes that sentence, writes it, carries it through the model, exposes it through the harness — and clips it off the bottom of the panel, then prints the word on a form two nodes later. A player answers ten questions about wounded dogs and toll-houses and is never told anything; they later find a noun on a document. Round 3 closed round 2's orphan-text defect on the questions and opened the same defect on the answer, and the round's own instrument certified it closed. That is the third time in this project a measurement has passed because it tested something adjacent to what the item asked for, and it is the exact failure BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 filed RI-JRN09 to prevent.

remedy.action: Two changes and a test, in this order. (1) Give the naming moment its own beat. The line is the payoff of a ten-node route and it is currently one entry in a `spoken` array that the layout treats as the least important thing on the panel. Add a node between the last question and writ.birthsign whose `line` IS the naming sentence and whose only input is an acknowledgement — the same shape writ.stamp was given this round for exactly this reason — so it occupies the one slot ui.js never sacrifices. Morrowind gives Socucius Ergalla his own beat to say 'you are a Battlemage'; this is that beat. (2) If the sacrifice loop is kept, make it declare what it dropped: have UILayer._redraw record the sacrificed lines in `metrics().sacrificed` so that any probe reading the surface can see the difference between 'not computed' and 'computed and thrown away'. Round 3's own defect is invisible in every instrument the build ships. (3) Fix tools/harness/jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 to test the naming LINE at the node it is spoken, not the class-name substring over the whole walk. The current test cannot go red while the writ draws the class name, which makes it a probe that cannot fail.

The substring reach test says 163 of 163. boot-check and check-content are green. Nineteen of nineteen pairs report both sides reachable. My own twelve chosen legs were 12/12. Only walking all forty-five documents in the loaded rooms found it — and the same collision will silently eat the next piece's placements, because nothing checks it. a-short-account-of-the-pacification is one half of the drowning-at-the-ford dispute, so the round's headline claim contains a counter-example nobody could have seen. gaps.what: The piece's detectors report PASS about things they did not sample, and its one detector that looks at the framebuffer rather than at the build's own register is looking at the wrong pixels. ui-forbidden.mjs is RI-UIX01 §B's OBSERVED probe — the only check in W1-21 that answers an AR-2 question from the picture instead of from getUIState() — and its first run against any build returns 66 digit glyphs over six enemies, all of which are helmet crests and jaw lines. It scans a 1280x720 coordinate space in a 1920x1080 frame because it never pins the drawing buffer; it grades a frame whose hit_frame is null, so the capture is not the post-hit frame the method requires; and its own self-test finds 10 glyphs where 3 were drawn. Around it, eleven of the fifteen graded checks across the five detectors return PASS on an empty sample set, three of them BY CONSTRUCTION on absence: FD7's `gradient_bits === null || >= 7`, FD6's edgeFringe() returning {worst: 0} with zero samples, and K4's bare `catch { continue }` on a missing state.
gaps.why_it_matters: docs/PLAN.md §3 makes this piece the enforcement point for the most-cited arbitration rule in the corpus, and round 2 has now genuinely closed the marker route it was failed for. What is left is worse in kind: the instruments are the only reason anyone would believe it stayed closed, and their green is not currently evidence. A detector that cannot distinguish an enemy's head from a damage number, in a set where most checks cannot distinguish 'nothing wrong' from 'nothing looked at', is how the next marker ships. The piece already knows the remedy — ui-census.mjs U7 and U10 are correctly guarded on a sample count, two lines from U8, which is not.

remedy.action: (a) ui-forbidden.mjs: call setDevicePixelRatio(1) before the first capture and assert screenshot().width === viewport.width; make hit_frame === null an exit 2 rather than a graded run; calibrate looksLikeDigit() against the --calibrate output rather than a hand-written band, since the self-test already draws the ground truth. gaps.what: The out-of-combat HUD has 1 of its 6 required elements, and the one element it has is in the wrong half of the screen. RI-UIX07 §B closes the world set at six: W1 bearing dial, W2 active-effect strip, W3 sneak state, W4 condition and charge marks on the quick slots, W5 place-name announcement, W6 breath meter. Only W1 exists — W2, W3, W4, W5 and W6 appear in no element-kind vocabulary on any frame captured, in any mode, across four separate runs. And W1's rect is [1782, 84, 96, 96], so y + h = 180 against H/2 = 540: it sits wholly in the top half, where §D1 requires the bottom half and §D2 requires the bottom-right corner or the rail inboard of it. Measured against the item's own §A, every persistent element of Morrowind's HUD is anchored Left Bottom or Right Bottom and the top of the screen is empty.
gaps.why_it_matters: For the ninety minutes of every hour the player is not fighting, the screen tells them their stamina — which they did not need — and nothing about where they are, which is the only question a markerless world poses; and the one element that would answer it is in the corner where a modern action-RPG puts its minimap, which is the register the whole interface is trying to stay out of.

remedy.action: Move the dial, then build the missing five cheapest-first. (1) In game/src/ui/compass.js, dialGeometry() computes cy = max(84*s + r, margin + r) — the top edge. Recompute it against the bottom edge so the dial anchors bottom-right, and where RI-UIX01's quick slots (E5, currently [1728,888,150,150]) and equip-load gauge (E9, [1758,852,120,24]) already hold that corner, place the dial immediately inboard on the same bottom rail; add the D4 overlap assertion against every RI-UIX01 rect. (2) Build W4 next because it costs nothing: a condition rule under the weapon slot and a cast-chance rule under the spell slot, drawn INSIDE E5's existing 150x150 rect, adding zero screen coverage — Morrowind draws both and they are visible as thin red rules in REF-A12c. (3) Then W3 sneak_state (40x40, both phases, only while hidden), W5 place_name (520x36, out of combat, <=3 s on cell change), W2 effect_strip (one glyph per active effect, <=12, growing leftward from the dial along the bottom edge), W6 breath_meter (400x24, both phases, only while submerged). (4) Add combat_phase, combat_phase_source: 'encounter' and frames_since_phase_change to getUIState(), read from the encounter state the AI reads and never recomputed in the UI layer, so V7 and V8 stop being proxy measurements.
remedy.acceptance: RI-UIX07 V1 reads 6 of 6: all six world-set kinds (bearing_dial, effect_strip, sneak_state, the condition/charge marks inside E5, place_name, breath_meter) appear in getUIState().elements under their declared conditions on a world frame, with the four refusals B1-B4 still held. V6 reads pass: every world-set element satisfies y + h > H/2 at 1920x1080 AND at 844x390, and intersects no RI-UIX01 element rect except W4, which is defined as being inside one. C3 world-set persistent coverage stays <= 1.5% and C4 union persistent stays <= 5.0% at 1920x1080 (the specified set computes to 0.52% and the shipped Souls set measures 2.49%, so the union has real headroom). And getUIState() returns a combat_phase field whose value on an aggro frame is 'fight' and on a quiet frame is 'world'.

gaps.what: One press of `confirm` on the journal's chronicle puts `focus.journal.view` into 'search', and no input in the build's own closed action set returns it. I drove all fifteen — roll, block, parry, heavy, sprint, jump, use_item, lock_on, two_hand, crouch, spell_cycle and all four movement axes — one at a time, through real DOM KeyboardEvents in mode `play-instrumented` with the input path asserted live (real.attached true, ArrowRight -> input.moveX 1). Fourteen leave `view === 'search'`; the fifteenth, `roll`, exits the entire screen to `world`. Walking back to the journal from any peer returns `view: 'search'` with the query intact, because neither `open()` nor `close()` resets `focus.journal`. The player has permanently lost the journal for the session by pressing the button the interface tells them to press. `backOrSub()` — defined at game/src/ui/system.js:711, which leaves the search view for the chronicle, then the index for the chronicle, then the screen, exactly as required — is CALLED NOWHERE in the tree. AND THE SCREEN PROMISES THE WAY OUT IN WRITING: the search view's own foot hint, photographed at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/T4-r2c/screens/critic-journal-stuck-search__1920x1080.png, reads 'Walk the letters, confirm to add one, BACK TO REMOVE ONE. Results are in the order they happened.' Back does not remove one. Back closes the journal. backOrSub()'s first branch is exactly that promise, implemented and unreachable — which makes this not a missing feature but a broken one, and the remedy a call site rather than a design.
gaps.why_it_matters: RI-UIX04 scores 11 of 12 on this same build and every one of its rows is about what the journal CONTAINS; none of them can see that the screen holding all of it can be shut in the player's face by one keystroke. That is the exact defect CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.2b was written for two days after the project shipped a dialogue window measuring ΔE 0.00 that the owner could not use, and it is the second instance of the same shape in the same week.

remedy.action: In `UISystem.step` (game/src/ui/system.js), change `if (!inCombat && input.pressedName('roll')) this.back();` to call `this.backOrSub()` — the method is already defined at line 711 and already leaves the search view for the chronicle, then the index for the chronicle, then the screen. Then reset `focus.journal.view` to 'chronicle' and `focus.journal.query` to '' inside `close()`, so a sub-view cannot survive a screen the player has shut.
remedy.acceptance: From `mode: 'journal'` with `focus.journal.view === 'search'` and a non-empty query, ONE real `roll` press removes one character; with an empty query it leaves `mode === 'journal'` with `focus.journal.view === 'chronicle'`; a further `roll` leaves the screen; and entering the journal from ANY of the peers in the walk ring returns `view: 'chronicle'`. `node tools/ui/t4-r2-critic-focus.mjs` must report JS1 and JS2 green (all 15 actions plus both axes enumerated), and the delete-the-fix arm — restore `this.back()` — must turn both red again, so the guard is proven to fail in both directions (HAZARDS §0b).

gaps.what: Every AR-2 detector this piece ships predates the map and none of them opens it — ui-layer's 8 viewpoints, ui-metrics' 6 screens, ui-forbidden's 4 menus, ui-census and marker-diff all stop at the six pre-S35 screens. The only compliance report on the surface S35 defines by its refusals is the one the map screen computes about itself, and the structural half of that report — getUIState().map.mutator_arities, the exact field AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-01 §3b tells a critic to read from the running object instead of trusting the source — is a hand-written literal of three method names that omits the object's fourth state-writing method, Discovery.restore(blob), arity 1, which names places by id and repaints the raster. Demonstrated end to end: a save whose world.discovery block is forged in both its fields loads with ZERO dropped, and the map draws 42 place squares, 35 of them for places the body has never stood in, over a fully rendered province, while the screen reports places_drawn == places_discovered == 42 and every check in the build stays green. map-probe.mjs L3 is the check that exists to catch this and it forges only the place list, leaving the raster honest — so the corroboration it performs is a fixed-point test on an input the same attacker controls.
gaps.why_it_matters: docs/PLAN.md §3 makes this piece the enforcement point for the most-cited arbitration rule in the corpus, and S35 moved the thing to be enforced from the journal to the map without the enforcement moving with it. The amended JU8 is nine assertions, seven of them hard fails, and the build tests none of them from outside the map's own code. AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-01 §3c states the rule this trips in advance: 'a map with a revealLocation(id) that nothing currently calls is not compliant, because the next quest author will find it and the check that catches them will be a code review rather than a number.' That is precisely the state the build is in — and the same shape (a compliance report assembled from a hand-written list, which can only report what its author already thought of) has now been caught in three separate pieces, twice in this one.

remedy.action: Four changes, in this order. (1) Put the map inside the detector suite: add ui_menu_map in BOTH the world and local views to ui-layer.mjs VIEWPOINTS; add `map` to ui-metrics.mjs SCREENS; add `map` to ui-forbidden.mjs's declared menu sweep; run marker-diff.mjs's quest-state differential with the map open as well as closed. (2) Replace the mutator_arities literal in game/src/ui/system.js with an enumeration over Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(sim.discovery)), classified by whether the method writes state, so a mutator nobody remembered is counted rather than omitted. (3) Close restore(): drop `places` from the save block entirely and re-derive the list on load from the raster plus the site radii in terrain.json sites[].r_flat — which deletes the forgeable field rather than validating it against another forgeable field. (4) Take ui-metrics.mjs's region selector off its four-kind whitelist, and make a screen whose stem sample count is zero a REPORTED FAILURE rather than a row filtered out of the median.
remedy.acceptance: ui-layer.mjs, ui-metrics.mjs, ui-forbidden.mjs and marker-diff.mjs each visit the map screen in both views and report 0 undeclared components, 0 forbidden kinds and 0 quest-conditioned elements there; getUIState().map.mutator_arities lists every state-writing method on the discovery prototype and every one of them has arity 0; ui-metrics.mjs reports a non-null stem sample count for all 7 screens it opens or names the screens it could not measure and exits non-zero; and node tools/harness/critic-w1-21-r1b.mjs returns F1, F2 and F3 PASS — a forged save naming all 42 places over an all-ones raster draws no more place squares than the body has stood in.

gaps.what: Every screen draws its panel at the same fixed rect [200, 160, 1520, 780] — 57.2% of a 1920x1080 frame — whatever it is holding, because game/src/ui/chrome.js:70 defines ONE constant BOX consumed by screenRect() and therefore by every screen through screen(). RI-UIX09 P4 requires D2 >= 0.35 of that rect to be matter and hard-fails below 0.15. Measured on captures I took at 7c63111d and sanity-checked with tools/visual/frame-liveness.mjs (8 frames, all LIVE): journal 0.1314, level-up 0.0910, sheet 0.0895, spells 0.0702, container 0.0572 — FIVE HARD FAILS — and inventory 0.1524, the only populated screen above the floor and still less than half the bar. Two independent implementations of the item's own method 4 agree to four decimals on all six screens. The arithmetic that matters is the good news inside it, re-derived here rather than quoted from S56: at the matter each screen ALREADY draws, D2 >= 0.35 is reached at 24.9% of frame for the inventory, 21.5% for the journal, 14.9% for level-up, 14.6% for the sheet, 11.5% for spells and 9.3% for the container. Morrowind's own inventory window is about 24% of its frame. This is a sizing defect, not a content defect, and round 3 reported it undone rather than half-done — it did not pad a number and it did not add decorative fill.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player opens the character sheet, the spell list, the level-up room or the journal and finds a room three-fifths furnished and two-fifths empty — six screens in a row that look unfinished, which is the first impression the interface makes and the one the owner will get in the first minute.

remedy.action: Replace game/src/ui/chrome.js:70's single `BOX = { x: 200, y: 160, w: 1520, h: 780 }` with a per-screen rect looked up by mode and consumed by screenRect(), then re-pitch each screen's absolute sc.inner offsets against its own box. TAKE THE FOUR CHEAP ONES FIRST — the journal (screens/text.js), the level-up screen and the character sheet (screens/progress.js) and the spell list all position against sc.inner in offsets that shrink cleanly, and the sheet additionally needs its skills column re-derived because it is written to FILL ih, which makes its contents height circular. LEAVE THE INVENTORY FOR A SECOND STEP: screens/inventory.js's COLS needs 200+20+132+24+640+30 = 1046 units of width before the detail panel gets any, so it cannot reach 24.9% by shrinking alone and needs its columns re-pitched, and it puts the worn band at iy + 476*s, the sort control at iy + 574*s and gold at iy + ih - 40*s, so any height below about 614 units collides.
remedy.acceptance: `node tools/ui/t4-r2-measure.mjs --out <dir>` then `node tools/ui/t4-r3-density.mjs --measure <dir> --out <reports>` reports `hard_fails: []` and `d2_critic >= 0.35` on journal, level-up, sheet and spells, with NO NEW DRAWN ELEMENT on any of them (each screen's `element_count` in measure-live-1920x1080.json unchanged within +/-2, so the fill comes from sizing and not from decorative filler). gaps.what: Protocol A re-ran five pairs after F1 (PBR materials), F2 (contact shadows + AO) and F3 (ambient/GI fill) all landed and each measured green on its own instrument — per orchestration/status/I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json: orphaned surface materials 321/422 to 0; contact-junction ratio 0.722 against a >=25% bar; ambient lift +0.631 replicated across three GPUs with the control at -0.001. The blind result did not move: 0 of 5 again, four judges at CONFIDENCE high and one at medium (unchanged spread from r1), and the aggregate synthesis of all five judges again names the same two absences r1 found — no material differentiation between surfaces ('every surface returns the same flat matte olive-grey', 'thatch, plaster, stone and ground all return light identically', 'nothing reads as leather, metal, stone or vegetation') and no contact darkening or cast shadow ('no contact darkening and no cast shadows at all, so nothing sits in space', 'surfaces meet with no contact darkening'). The mechanical local_contrast_med statistic still sweeps 5/5 toward the reference on the same channel r1's leak-check also swept 5/5.
gaps.why_it_matters: The remedies exist in the codebase and pass their own numeric gates, but a player looking at the world still sees what the r1 judges saw: every surface responding to light the same way, and nothing casting a contact shadow. An instrument passing its own gate has stopped being evidence that the player-visible problem is fixed, which is exactly the failure RI-VIS06 exists to catch.

gaps.what: The anti-gaming guard on the character defect metric is a scalar silhouette-area check, and a scalar cannot notice that a named part stopped existing. Deleting both of the character's hands — palms, three fingers and an opposed thumb each — improves the headline crack metric by 31% and moves the guarded quantity by 0.31% against a 3.0% threshold. It is not caught.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every claim this piece makes about the character rests on the crack metric, and the crack metric's only defence against being gamed has now been shown, on a copy of the source tree, to miss the cheapest realistic mutilation. The builder's two declared cheats — delete a whole arm, swallow the arms into the torso — are the conspicuous versions and they are caught. The version a builder under schedule pressure would actually reach for is deleting the small expensive parts, and that walks straight through. The plan's own item 5 calls hands one of the two features a person looks at first.

remedy.action: Replace the scalar silhouette-area guard with a PER-PART PRESENCE CENSUS in tools/visual/actor-hole-control.mjs, and keep the area guard as its second half. rasterise() in actor-orbit-holes.mjs already carries owner[] and the part label, so classifyPockets's caller can record the set of part names contributing at least one pixel anywhere in the run and return it on the summary. The comparison tool then fails any build whose part set is a strict subset of the baseline's. Roughly a dozen lines and no new threshold to argue about. gaps.what: The moveset animation model — 1150 distinct clips over 2689 slots and 87 weapons, the solved arcs, the solved blade lengths, the 25-slot contract — has no renderer. `grep -rn "weapon" game/src/render/` returns nothing, `grep -rn "bone" game/src/render/` returns nothing, and no SkinnedMesh is constructed anywhere in game/src. `game/src/render/scene.js` makeActor() builds a rigid group of nine primitives — torso, head, snout, hips, two static legs, two static arms — plus `new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.055, 0.95, 0.014)` welded at local (0.40, 1.28, 0.10) as 'the blade', one 0.95 m box for all eighty-seven weapons. `game/src/render/renderer.js:398-399` is the whole of the player's animation: playerMesh.position.set(sim.player.pos) and playerMesh.rotation.y = yaw. Measured in the shipping build: across a full 60-frame r1.1, the character-box pixel change is 0.19% peak for hlb_garrison_bill (2.85 m, a 146.8 deg sweep over 14 active frames) and 0.21% for cgs_drowned_reaper (a `spin` over 18 active frames); ssw_garrison_sword's 2.4% is flat from f030 to f060 and is the root lunge translating a rigid mesh, not a swing. Frame-0 screenshots of ssw_garrison_sword (1.95 m), hlb_garrison_bill (2.85 m) and cgs_drowned_reaper (2.75 m) are byte-identical, md5 9bdb823fbcdb3ba820b2946b05ffa55a.
gaps.why_it_matters: WEAPON-CRITIC 0 states this role's whole subject: 'the deficit lives entirely in the animation-clip column of the moveset data and in the root tracks the clips produce.' ARBITRATION 3's CONSUMPTION check states the consequence: 'a model with no demonstrated consumer is unmeasurable => 0, exactly as a missing model is — from the player's chair they are the same thing', and it lists 'character creation rendered 20 byte-identical screenshots while returning correct values' as one of the four wave-1 instances. This is that instance again, in the area the check was written for. Round 1 found the 87 movesets unreachable from the running game; round 3 made them reachable to the hitbox solver; they are still unreachable to the screen. The builder demonstrated a consumer for the IMPACT model, correctly and convincingly, and never asked the same question of the ANIMATION model — whose only consumer is the solver that grades it. It is also the mechanism by which every other defect here survived three rounds: the blade points 35-52 degrees into the ground and sits 100% below the floor plane through the entire damaging window of CGS, HLB, TSW and WHP (so a halberd lands nothing at 2.65 m and nothing at all against a retreating target), and that is invisible to a critic who cannot see the swing and unmissable to anyone who can. gaps.what: The RI-WPN05 impact and material model is a data island, exactly as the 87 movesets were in round 1. Five of six perturbations of the shipped tables change nothing in the fight: setting every non-flesh cell of the 5x7 attacker hitstop grid to 99 f, setting every material damage multiplier to 0.01, setting every knockback value to 9 m, and setting the deflection multiplier to 20x all produce a byte-identical fight (dmg 118, hit at frame 32, hitstop held 3 frames). Only the flesh column is read, and it is read from a hard-coded `.flesh` lookup at game/src/combat/moves.js:166. MovesetLibrary.materialMultiplier, .deflects, .knockbackFor and .victimHitstopFor are imported by exactly one file in the repository — game/src/harness/weapons.js, the harness. gaps.why_it_matters: This is round 1's verdict repeating itself one layer down, and it is invisible for the same reason: the builder fixed the half of the piece the round-1 gap named and the impact half was never examined, so every probe that reads the library reports a healthy 5x7 grid. The material system is also this area's ONLY seam crossing under AR-3: a lore fact (root-golems are stone, the Hist-bonded are plant) that is supposed to be a combat answer a merchant can sell you. Unread, the crossing does not exist, and the weapon area becomes internally excellent and externally sterile.

gaps.what: All thirteen regions are the same three primitives — canopy, under, rock — recoloured, and not one of the thirteen declared ONLY-HERE elements exists in the world. Every region in game/data/world/regions.json carries the identical prop schema `canopy+under+rock`, drawing on seven shared canopy shapes and five shared under shapes; the whole 14.31 km2 province renders with textureMB 0, atlasCount 0, 17 materials and 8 programs. `only_here: {id, instances}` — welkynd_pillar x34, petrified_bole x400, rock_flute_spire x14, glassed_crater x16, beached_hull_house x12 and nine more — is an integer literal in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and nothing places an instance, so RI-WLD04 M19 measures 0 of 13. Five of M18's nine axes (fauna, architecture, audio, weather, hazard) are DROPPED rather than measured, which is the same statement in the instrument's own words. The consequence is measurable two ways. A human taking M17 on the now-honest pack scores 4/8 against a pass bar of 85%, and three of the four misses are one miss: frames 023, 042 and 050 are the Stone Wastes — 'glassed salt crust', glass_thorn, whale_bone_frame, salt_block_wall, crater_rim — and all three read as Marauder's Coast, because what is rendered is a khaki flat under a white fog band. And with colour and exposure removed from the machine descriptor, leave-one-out identification falls 74.4% -> 30.8% and Fisher 3.10 -> 1.77: about two-thirds of the measured region separability is carried by tint alone, which is RI-WLD04's own named way to lose.
gaps.why_it_matters: S24 rules that thirteen regions must each read as a different place and that an implementation where everything is one terrain with a recoloured fog has failed regardless of how good the terrain is — and a player walking the 6.6 km crossing passes through five regions that differ in ground colour and in nothing they can name.

remedy.action: Place the ONLY-HERE elements as real instances, and give each region at least one prop class that no other region has. Concretely: (1) extend the region prop schema in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and game/src/world/province.js beyond `canopy+under+rock` with a fourth slot `signature`, carrying its own mesh generator per region — a welkynd pillar for Blackwood, a rock-flute spire for Valus Ridge, a whale-bone frame and crater rim for the Stone Wastes, a beached hull house and tide pole for Marauder's Coast, a drowned xanmeer tooth and corpse lily for the Deep Marshes, a stilt row and tideway marker for the Eastern Rootlands; (2) place them at the counts regions.json already declares, from the same seeded lattice the existing props use, so the number in the table becomes the number in the world; (3) add a `signature_silhouette` axis and an `architecture_placed` axis to tools/world/region-axes.mjs, computed from placed instances rather than from a table row, and un-drop `architecture`; (4) give the ground more than one material — at present textureMB is 0, so albedo is a per-region constant and RI-WLD04's 'albedo must come from different materials, not a LUT' cannot be satisfied at all.

gaps.what: The trunk road network is routed along the floors of water bodies. Sampling getWaterAt() at every point of all ten built legs at tide LOW: 1,364 m of road (5.4%) is above knee depth and 574 m (2.3%) is above chest depth, concentrated on the Stormhold-Helstrom leg, which carries 538 m over-knee and 502 m over-chest and reaches a maximum depth of 65.64 m at (2182.52, 2214.63) - ground at 69.66 m under a water surface at 135.30 m. That leg is the first of THE CROSSING, so 502 m of the canonical 6,788 m walk - 7.4%, about 4.2 minutes of the hour - is walked along a lake bed.
